## Abstract

Combining inhibition of poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase and androgen receptor (AR) pathway has demonstrated clinical activity in men with metastatic prostate cancer, although the extent of benefit in tumors lacking homologous recombination repair (HRR) gene alterations remains uncertain. We conducted a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating talazoparib plus enzalutamide versus enzalutamide alone in men with high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC). Fifty-four patients starting androgen deprivation therapy received two cycles of enzalutamide lead-in before 1:2 randomization to enzalutamide (n = 17) or enzalutamide plus talazoparib (n = 37). The primary endpoint was met, with a 73% prostate-specific antigen (PSA) <0.2 ng ml−1 response rate at 12 months in the combination arm (95% confidence interval (CI) = 56–86%), exceeding the prespecified efficacy threshold (P < 0.001); the PSA <0.2 rate in the control arm was 64.7% (95% CI = 38–86%, P = 0.54 for exploratory comparison between arms). Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 68% patients receiving the combination versus 35% with enzalutamide alone, predominantly anemia (41%). Two fatal therapy-emergent myeloid neoplasms occurred in the enzalutamide plus talazoparib arm in patients with underlying genomic susceptibility. Analyses of paired tumor biopsies acquired at baseline and during enzalutamide lead-in phase demonstrated marked tumor transcriptional reprogramming after AR inhibition, including suppression of proliferation-associated and HRR-related gene expression programs, but without functional impairment of homologous recombination activity. Overall, talazoparib plus enzalutamide demonstrated clinical activity in patients with high-volume mHNPC but did not establish clear additional clinical benefit over enzalutamide alone in this biomarker-unselected population, while being associated with increased toxicity. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT04332744.

In the metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer (mHNPC) setting, multiple phase 3 trials have reshaped the therapeutic landscape, demonstrating that intensifying androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) combined with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) significantly improves overall survival (OS) and delays progression to metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC)2,3,4,5,6. cases.text: BACKGROUND: OCEANIC-STROKE (XXX) showed that asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing bleeding in patients with noncardioembolic ischemic stroke or high-risk transient ischemic attack. We characterized bleeding categories, sites, and key subgroups. METHODS: In the safety population, 12 254 participants received at least 1 dose of asundexian (n=6124) or placebo (n=6130). Bleeding was categorized by International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis criteria as major, clinically relevant nonmajor (CRNM), or minor. While-on-treatment analyses included events through 2 days after the last dose, with death and permanent discontinuation as competing risks. RESULTS: Major bleeding occurred in 117 (1.9%) participants with asundexian and 107 (1.7%) with placebo (cause-specific hazard ratio [csHR], 1.10 [95% CI, 0.85–1.44]; P =0.46). Major or CRNM bleeding occurred in 339 (5.5%) and 307 (5.0%), respectively (csHR, 1.12 [95% CI, 0.96–1.30]; P =0.16), and any bleeding in 763 (12.5%) and 752 (12.3%) (csHR, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.93–1.13]; P =0.65). Treatment effects for major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups, including planned dual antiplatelet therapy. Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in 41 (0.7%) and 36 (0.6%) participants. Any gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in 186 (3.0%) and 147 (2.4%) (csHR, 1.28 [95% CI, 1.03–1.59]), and lower gastrointestinal bleeding in 102 (1.7%) and 59 (1.0%) (csHR, 1.75 [95% CI, 1.27–2.41]), primarily rectal bleeding. Any procedure-related bleeding and any mucosal bleeding did not differ significantly. CONCLUSIONS: Asundexian added to antiplatelet therapy reduced ischemic stroke without significantly increasing major, major or CRNM, or any bleeding. Lower gastrointestinal bleeding was more frequent with asundexian, whereas treatment effects on major and major or CRNM bleeding were consistent across prespecified subgroups. item.titleZh: 影像筛选下超4.5小时静脉溶栓：更新系统评价与Meta分析

cases.text: BACKGROUND: Intravenous thrombolysis is a standard treatment for acute ischemic stroke but has traditionally been limited to 4.5 hours after symptom onset. This time-based restriction may exclude patients with salvageable brain tissue, especially those with wake-up or unknown-onset strokes. Multimodal imaging allows for the identification of viable penumbra beyond traditional treatment windows. This study compiles randomized evidence evaluating intravenous thrombolysis in imaging-selected patients treated after 4.5 hours. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses guidelines. PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central were searched through February 2026 for randomized trials comparing intravenous thrombolysis (alteplase or tenecteplase) with best medical therapy in patients presenting beyond 4.5 hours or with wake-up/unknown-onset stroke selected by imaging. The primary outcome was excellent functional outcome at 90 days (modified Rankin Scale score 0–1). Secondary outcomes included functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0–2), symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, and 90-day mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen trials involving 4192 participants were analyzed. Intravenous thrombolysis improved excellent functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–1; risk ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.16–1.29]) and functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score 0–2; risk ratio, 1.12 [95% CI, 1.06–1.18]). Both alteplase and tenecteplase contributed to these benefits. Thrombolysis increased the risk of symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (risk ratio, 2.58 [95% CI, 1.58–4.22]) but did not significantly affect 90-day mortality (risk ratio, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.97–1.35]). CONCLUSIONS: In patients selected using advanced imaging, intravenous thrombolysis performed after 4.5 hours improves functional outcomes without increasing mortality, supporting a tissue-based rather than strictly time-based approach to treating acute ischemic stroke.

This work is licensed under a CC BY 4.0 License

## Background

This study retrospectively analyzed the treatment outcomes of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery.

## Methods

Patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery who underwent CT-guided BT between were retrospectively analyzed. The primary endpoint was local control (LC). Secondary endpoints included regional recurrence-free survival (RRFS), distant metastasis-free survival (DMFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities.

## Results

50 patients were included. External beam radiotherapy (EBRT) with a median total dose of 50 Gy was administered to 30 patients. The median number of BT fractions was five for patients with superficial recurrence and three for those with visible recurrence, respectively. The median total dose delivered to the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) (equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions; EQD2) was 70.5 Gy. The median follow-up period was 44.8 months. The 3-year LC, RRFS, DMFS, DFS, and OS rates were 85.6%, 82.9%, 65.1%, 46.0%, and 87.1%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, HR-CTV D90 was a significant prognostic factor for LC (p = 0.009). The 3-year LC rate was significantly higher in patients with HR-CTV D90 ≥ 67.3 Gy than in those with < 67.3 Gy (100% vs. 64.2%). In the multivariate analysis, tumor visibility and postoperative risk classification were significant prognostic factors for DMFS (p < 0.011 and p = 0.033, respectively).

## Conclusions

CT-guided BT provides favorable local control in patients with vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. However, distant metastases remain a major site of failure.

Not applicable.

The first-line treatment for endometrial cancer is generally surgical management. Postoperative adjuvant therapy is administered considering the risk of recurrence determined by postoperative pathological findings. Considering the results of previous clinical trials on adjuvant therapy after surgery [1, 2], adjuvant chemotherapy after surgery has been widely adopted in Japan to reduce the risk of distant metastasis [3]. Although some patients who undergo postoperative radiotherapy (RT) experience vaginal recurrence [2, 4, 5], vaginal recurrence is associated with a more favorable prognosis than recurrence at other metastasis sites [4, 6]. RT is recommended as a treatment option for postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer in patients without a prior history of RT [7].

Postoperative vaginal recurrence is often treated with brachytherapy (BT). Recently, image-guided brachytherapy (IGBT) using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and computed tomography (CT) has been increasingly adopted in clinical practice. Several reports have described the outcomes of RT for postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer, demonstrating favorable local control rates [8, 9]. However, there are few reports on the use of IGBT for vaginal recurrence after endometrial cancer surgery. Furthermore, until recently, the definition of the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) for BT in postoperative vaginal recurrence of endometrial cancer remained unclear. Although MRI-guided BT target definition guidelines for recurrent endometrial and cervical tumors were published in 2023 [10], CT-guided BT continues to be used for gynecologic cancers at some institutions.

Therefore, this study aimed to retrospectively analyze the treatment outcomes of CT-guided BT for vaginal recurrence after endometrioid cancer surgery and to establish future treatment strategies.

## Patients and eligibility

Patients with vaginal recurrence after surgery for endometrial cancer who underwent BT at least once at our institution between January 2014 and June 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients who underwent external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) before BT at hospitals related to our institution were included. The main eligibility criteria were as follows: age 20 years or more; histological diagnosis of endometrioid carcinoma, clear cell carcinoma, or serous carcinoma; no distant metastases other than paraaortic and inguinal lymph node metastasis at the time of vaginal recurrence diagnosis; and no history of pelvic radiotherapy.

## The detection of vaginal recurrence at imaging examination

Vaginal recurrence identified by visual examination was confirmed by cytology or histological evaluation in the present study. However, recurrent tumors were detectable on imaging examinations, such as CT and MRI, in some patients, but not in others. Because the RT strategy differed considerably according to whether the recurrent tumor was detectable on imaging, patients were categorized as having non-visible recurrence when the tumor was not detectable on imaging and visible recurrence when the tumor was detectable. Therefore, the primary focus of this analysis was the imaging detectability of recurrent tumors.

## External beam radiotherapy

In some patients, a combination of EBRT and BT was administered at the discretion of the clinician. Three-dimensional conformal radiotherapy (3DCRT) or volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) was administered. Depending on the treatment indication, either whole pelvic (WP) irradiation or localized vaginal irradiation was performed. ## Abstract

Introduction Adolescents experience high rates of depression and anxiety, yet globally 80% of adolescents and almost all in low-and middle-income countries (LMICs) lack access to adolescent-friendly treatments. The African Youth in Mind (Y-MIND) set out to adapt the youth version of the Friendship Bench and assess its feasibility for delivery in Ghana.

Methods In this feasibility cluster randomised controlled trial, we recruited participants aged 15–18 years with probable diagnosis of moderate to severe depression ascertained with the Patient Health Questionnaire (PHQ-9) total score > 9 from six Senior High Schools in Navrongo, Ghana. Schools were randomly allocated (1:2) to enhanced usual care (EUC) alone or EUC combined with Y-MIND, prior to recruitment of participants. Primary outcomes were feasibility (intervention delivery; conducting a fully powered trial). Secondary outcomes were intervention appropriateness, acceptability, and probable depression symptom severity and remission on the PHQ-9.

Results Between July and August 2024, we enrolled and allocated 67 participants (43 [64%] to the EUC plus Y-MIND group and 24 [36%] to the EUC alone group), of whom 64 (95.5%) completed the 5-month primary outcome assessment (41 [95.3%] in the EUC plus Y-MIND group and 23 [95.8%] in the EUC alone group). The feasibility of delivering the Y-MIND intervention from the perspective of adolescents had a mean score of 4.3 (0.5). Therapy quality score was 94.8% (95% CI: 93.0–96.6), while therapy competence was 86.6% (95% CI: 81.2–92.2). We observed initial clinical benefits, including lower severity of depressive symptoms among adolescents in the Y-MIND group as compared to those in the EUC group, with most participants achieving symptomatic remission at the month 5 follow-up.

Conclusion The Y-MIND school-based psychological treatment model demonstrated good acceptability and feasibility, with high recruitment, retention, treatment adherence, and provider competence. While preliminary findings indicate potential improvements in depressive symptoms, the study was not designed to establish effectiveness. These findings justify progression to a fully powered trial to determine clinical effectiveness, cost-effectiveness, and the scalability of the intervention within routine school settings in LMICs. Trial registration: Clinicaltrials.gov (NCT06740084).

## Dynamics of a slow-burn epidemic: the genomic epidemiology of poultry-associated Campylobacter jejuni ST474 in New Zealand

View ORCID ProfileN.P. French, D.A. Wilkinson, View ORCID ProfileP.J. Biggs, View ORCID ProfileA.C. Midwinter, View ORCID ProfileJ.M Collins-Emerson, View ORCID ProfileA. doi: https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.10.09.26364997

- Abstract - Full Text - Info/History - Metrics - Data/Code - Preview PDF

## ABSTRACT

The emergence of a dominant poultry-associated strain of Campylobacter jejuni in New Zealand coincided with a multi-year epidemic of human campylobacteriosis. This was characterised by an increase in cases to 2006, when one of the highest national case-rates in the world was recorded, followed by a rapid decline attributed to interventions in the poultry industry. The strain belonged to an internationally rare multilocus sequence type, ST474 - a member of Clonal Complex (CC) 48 - that was highly prevalent in both poultry and human cases in New Zealand but was also identified in other samples. ST474 isolates from humans, animal reservoirs and environmental water samples were collected between 2005 and 2019 and whole genome sequenced (N=443). Isolates from a 2018/9 case-control study of campylobacteriosis in New Zealand were included for genomic comparisons with other sequence types and CCs. This presented an opportunity to examine the genomic epidemiology of a single, relatively recently emerged lineage of C. jejuni, and improve our understanding of drivers of emergence and persistence in a relatively isolated ecosystem.

Six subpopulations (clades) of ST474 were identified and these varied in terms of their host association, persistence, patterns of homologous recombination, and complement of mobile genetic elements, including plasmids and chromosomally integrated elements. Clade E was associated with a single poultry supplier in the initial epidemic phase and accounted for 34.5% of human cases. Clade F emerged from a declining Clade E after the peak in human cases and was also associated with poultry. The emergence of Clade F was accompanied by the loss of integrated element CJIE5 and the acquisition of multiple blocks of recombination, likely from diverse ancestral C. jejuni lineages, and the loss of the methionine biosynthesis operon metAB. In contrast, Clades A-D were detected at low frequencies in human cases over the 14-year period of surveillance and were associated with multiple hosts. This longitudinal study sheds light on the evolutionary processes that result in strain emergence and differentiation, highlighting the role of horizontal gene transfer in the evolution and adaptation of this pathogen to new niches, and the subsequent impact on public health.

item.titleRaw: Clinical practice guidelines: management of non-post-operative supra-ventricular tachycardia in neonates and children less than 18 years old hospitalized in a Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
item.titleZh: 儿童非术后室上性心动过速管理指南

cases.text: PURPOSE: We present guidelines in the form of pragmatic recommendations for management of neonates and children less than 18 years old presenting with non-post-operative supraventricular tachycardia (SVT) and hospitalized in a Paediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU). METHODS: Thirteen French-speaking experts, all of them members of the Groupe Francophone de Réanimation et Urgence Pédiatriques (French-speaking group of paediatric intensive and emergency care; GFRUP), collaborated from 2024 to 2025 through teleconferences and face-to-face meetings. The guidelines cover four areas: (1) epidemiology and criteria for admission to a PICU, (2) paraclinical assessment, (3) non-specific rhythm management, and (4) specific rhythm management. The questions were formulated in the Patient-Intervention-Comparison-Outcome (PICO) format. An extensive Anglophone and Francophone literature search indexed in the MEDLINE database via PubMed, Cochrane and Embase was performed using pre-established keywords. The texts were analyzed and classified according to the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) methodology. When this method was not applicable, an expert opinion was given. Each of the recommendations was voted on by all the experts according to the Delphi methodology. RESULTS: The group proposes 21 recommendations. The GRADE methodology could be applied for five of them, and an expert opinion was given for the remaining 16. All of the recommendations received strong approval. CONCLUSION: These guidelines cover different aspects in the management of non-post-operative SVT in children hospitalized in PICUs including non-specific and specific rhythm management.

item.titleRaw: Health Bureau announces commencement of patient pairing arrangements under Community Pharmacy Programme (Community) and annual consultation co-payment adjustments of Primary Healthcare Co-care Network
item.titleZh: 香港公布社区药房计划患者配对安排及共付额调整

cases.text:
Health Bureau announces commencement of patient pairing arrangements under Community Pharmacy Programme (Community) and annual consultation co-payment adjustments of Primary Healthcare Co-care Network

******************************************************************************************

CPP (Community)'s patient pairing arrangements

To implement the Primary Healthcare Blueprint's recommendations of adopting a multidisciplinary approach for the proper management of chronic diseases in the community, strengthen the professional role of community pharmacists, and provide patients with more options for drug dispensing or refill services, as well as medication counselling and management services in the community, the first phase of the CPP (Community) will be piloted at four districts to launch patient pairing arrangements for designated family doctors participating in the Co-care Network and Family Medicine Clinics of the Hospital Authority (HA), with a total of 20 designated pharmacies across the districts. Upon successful pairing, participating patients will be able to obtain drugs from their preferred pharmacy, with pharmacists providing medication counselling and related drug and health advice, thereby enhancing patients' drug compliance and personal health management. Drug refill services at community pharmacies can also help prevent the accumulation of excess drugs at home by patients, reducing the risk of improper storage and misuse while minimising potential drug wastage.

The first phase of the programme will be piloted at four districts, namely Eastern, Yau Tsim Mong, Sha Tin and Yuen Long, with five community pharmacies conveniently located near residential areas and shopping malls selected in each district (list set out in Annex). The HHB will invite, in phases, family doctors participating in the Co-care Network to join the programme, and will invite eligible patients to enrol and be paired with a designated community pharmacy of their choice, and brief them on details of the drug dispensing or refill arrangements. In future, the second phase of the programme will cover Southern, Wong Tai Sin, Kwun Tong, Tuen Mun, North and Tai Po districts, while the third phase will cover the remaining eight districts. The HHB will extend services to all 18 districts across the city in the fourth quarter of next year. More eligible pharmacies in each district will also be invited to join the programme thereafter.

For those using community pharmacies under the programme, drug co-payment for Co-care Network participants will be charged in accordance with the arrangements of the Community Drug Formulary, while drug fees for HA patients will remain aligned with the HA's prevailing fee schedule. More details on the Community Drug Formulary and the operation of the CPP (Community) will be announced in due course.

Co-care Network's annual consultation co-payment adjustments

Under the co-payment model of the Co-care Network, the Government provides a partial subsidy, while participants are required to pay a certain amount of co-payment fee, with a view to encouraging citizens to bear the primary responsibility for their own health. Participating family doctors are allowed to determine the consultation co-payment fees for the screening phase (not more than $120 for cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and not more than $180 for chronic hepatitis B screening) and the treatment phase on their own, and have the fees adjusted once annually according to the established mechanism. The list of consultation co-payment fees for the screening and treatment phases taking effect from November 1 has been uploaded to the dedicated website of the Co-care Network for public reference. Relevant information on the webpage for searching family doctors will also be updated on the same day.

Regarding the treatment phase, following the co-payment fee adjustment, the proportion of service points charging consultation co-payment fees at or below the Government-recommended level of $150 will remain above 60 per cent (773 service points), while the median co-payment remains at $150. Among the current 1 239 participating service points, 1 022 of them (i.e. 82.5 per cent) will keep their existing co-payment fees unchanged. Twenty-eight service points will reduce their co-payment fees (the median reduction is $100), while the remaining 189 service points will increase their co-payment fees, of which nearly 90 per cent will raise their fees by $50 or below. Overall, the rate of increase of the consultation co-payment fees for the treatment phase is 3.7 per cent in the coming year. For the co-payment fees for the screening phase, the vast majority of service points (over 97 per cent) will charge the Government-recommended co-payment levels. In addition, 28 and 20 service points will charge co-payments below the Government-recommended level for cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and chronic hepatitis B screening respectively.

As at October 7 (Note 1) this year, more than 300 000 citizens have enrolled in the Co-care Network. Among the participants who have completed cardiovascular disease risk factor screening and/or chronic hepatitis B screening, around 70 000 have been diagnosed with cardiovascular disease risk factors (i.e. suffering from diabetes mellitus, hypertension or hyperlipidaemia, or prediabetes (Note 2)) and/or chronic hepatitis B, and have entered the treatment phase.

For more details of the CPP, members of the public may visit its dedicated website or call the hotline at 2525 2328. For more details of the Co-care Network, members of the public may visit its dedicated website or call the hotline at 2157 0500. Dedicated staff of both hotlines will answer calls from 9am to 9pm from Monday to Saturday.

Note 1: These are provisional figures, subject to revision upon the availability of updated data.

Note 2: Prediabetes refers to HbA1c levels of 6.0-6.4 per cent or FPG levels of 6.1-6.9 mmol/

2023年8月9日，美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）对普拉替尼（Gavreto，Genentech, Inc.）给予常规批准，用于经FDA批准的检测方法检出转染重排（RET）融合阳性的转移性非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）成人患者。普拉替尼此前于2020年9月4日基于ARROW试验（NCT03037385，一项多中心、开放标签、多队列试验）中入组的114例患者的初始总缓解率（ORR）和缓解持续时间（DOR）获得NSCLC适应证的加速批准。转为常规批准是基于另外123例患者的数据以及额外25个月的随访，以评估缓解的持久性。查看Gavreto的完整处方信息。疗效在共计237例局部晚期或转移性RET融合阳性NSCLC患者中得到证实。患者接受普拉替尼治疗直至疾病进展或出现不可接受的毒性。主要疗效指标为盲态独立审查委员会（BIRC）判定的ORR和DOR。在107例初治患者中，ORR为78%（95% CI：68，85），中位DOR为13.4个月（95% CI：9.4，23.1）。在130例既往接受过含铂化疗的患者中，ORR为63%（95% CI：54，71），中位DOR为38.8个月（95% CI：14.8，不可估计）。最常见的不良反应（≥ 25%）为肌肉骨骼疼痛、便秘、高血压、腹泻、疲乏、水肿、发热和咳嗽。普拉替尼的推荐剂量为400 mg口服，每日一次。普拉替尼应空腹服用（服用普拉替尼前至少2小时和服用后至少1小时内不进食）。本审评使用了Assessment Aid，这是申请人自愿提交以促进FDA审评的材料。本申请获得了突破性疗法认定和孤儿药认定。

FDA快速通道项目在《行业指南：严重疾病的快速通道项目——药物和生物制品》中有所描述。医疗专业人员应将所有怀疑与任何药物和器械使用相关的严重不良事件报告至FDA的MedWatch报告系统，或致电1-800-FDA-1088。如需在研肿瘤产品单患者IND方面的协助，医疗专业人员可联系OCE的Project Facilitate，电话240-402-0004，或发送电子邮件至OncProjectFacilitate@fda.hhs.gov。在X（原Twitter）上关注肿瘤卓越中心@FDAOncology。

item.titleZh: 欧洲药品管理局EPAR更新：舒格利单抗Cejemly获批用于非小细胞肺癌

cases.text:
- Application under evaluation

- CHMP opinion

- European Commission decision

Overview

Cejemly is a cancer medicine used in adults to treat a lung cancer called non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). It is used:

- in patients whose cancer has spread to other parts of the body (metastatic) and when genetic mutations in the genes for EGFR, ALK, ROS1 or RET are not present. It is used together with platinum-based chemotherapy (other cancer medicines);

- in patients whose cancer has spread within the lung (stage III) and cannot be removed by surgery (unresectable), and whose disease has not worsened after treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy plus radiation therapy. Cejemly is used when the cancer produces a certain amount of a protein called PD-L1 and when genetic mutations in the genes for EGFR, ALK or ROS1 are not present.

Cejemly contains the active substance sugemalimab.

Treatment with Cejemly should be started and supervised by a doctor experienced in the use of cancer medicines. The medicine can only be obtained with a prescription.

Cejemly is given as an infusion (drip) into a vein over 60 minutes every 3 weeks.

Treatment with Cejemly should continue until it stops working. The doctor may interrupt treatment if certain side effects occur or stop it altogether for certain severe side effects.

For more information about using Cejemly, see the package leaflet or contact your doctor or pharmacist.

The active substance in Cejemly, sugemalimab, is a monoclonal antibody (a type of protein) designed to attach to a protein called PD-L1 found on some cancer cells. Cancer cells use this PD‑L1protein to bind to certain receptors on the surface of T cells (cells of the immune system). This blocks the activity of T cells and prevents them from attacking the cancer. By attaching to the PD-L1 protein on the cancer cells, sugemalimab stops them from blocking the T cell activity. This increases the ability of the immune system to kill the cancer cells.

Two main studies found that Cejemly increased the time people with non-small cell lung cancer lived without their disease getting worse.

Metastatic NSCLC

A main study involved 479 adults with metastatic NSCLC with no changes affecting the EGFR, ALK, ROS1 or RET genes. They received either Cejemly or placebo (a dummy treatment), each given together with platinum-based chemotherapy. The study found that people who received Cejemly lived for an average of 9 months before their cancer got worse compared with 5 months for people who received placebo. Overall, people who received Cejemly with chemotherapy lived for around 25 months, while those who received placebo with chemotherapy lived for around 17 months.

Locally advanced unresectable NSCLC

Another main study involved 381 adults with NSCLC that has spread within the lung and cannot be removed by surgery and whose disease has not worsened after treatment with platinum-based chemotherapy plus radiation therapy. People included in the study received either Cejemly or placebo and the study found that people who received Cejemly lived for an average of 10.6 months before their cancer got worse compared with 6.2 months for people who received placebo. Results showed no significant difference in survival between those who had the treatment and those who did not.

For the full list of side effects and restrictions with Cejemly, see the package leaflet.

The most common side effects with Cejemly (which may affect more than 1 in 10 people) include anaemia (low levels of red blood cells), increased levels of liver enzymes, rash, hyperlipidaemia (high blood fat levels), hyperglycaemia (high blood glucose levels), hyponatraemia (low blood levels of sodium), hypokalaemia (low blood levels of potassium), hypothyroidism (an underactive thyroid gland), hyperthyroidism (an overactive thyroid gland), proteinuria (protein in urine), abdominal (belly) pain, tiredness, arthralgia (joint pain), hypoaesthesia (reduced sensation to touch, pain and temperature) and hypocalcaemia (low blood levels of calcium).

Cejemly is also commonly associated with side effects related to the activity of the immune system on body organs. Most will resolve with appropriate treatment or after interrupting or stopping Cejemly.

Cejemly was shown to increase the time people with metastatic or advanced, unresectable non-small cell lung cancer live without their disease getting worse. For the use in metastatic disease Cejemly also increased the time they lived overall. The use of Cejemly in patients with locally advanced NSCLC after platinum-based chemotherapy and radiotherapy is restricted to those whose cancer produces PD-L1, since a clear benefit was only shown in this group of patients. The safety profile of Cejemly was manageable and no new safety concerns were identified. The European Medicines Agency therefore decided that Cejemly’s benefits are greater than its risks and that it can be authorised for use in the EU.

The company that markets Cejemly will provide a patient card about side effects affecting the immune system and when to seek help if these occur. This card will also inform healthcare professionals that the patient is being treated with Cejemly.

Recommendations and precautions to be followed by healthcare professionals and patients for the safe and effective use of Cejemly have also been included in the summary of product characteristics and the package leaflet.

As for all medicines, data on the use of Cejemly are continuously monitored. Suspected side effects reported with Cejemly are carefully evaluated and any necessary action taken to protect patients.

Cejemly received a marketing authorisation valid throughout the EU on 24 July 2024.

This medicine’s product information is available in all official EU languages.

Select 'available languages' to access the language you need.

- summary of product characteristics (annex I);

item.titleRaw: Hibsago (bepirovirsen) approved in the US for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB)
item.titleZh: bepirovirsen获美国FDA批准用于慢性乙肝治疗

cases.text:
Issued: London, UK

For investors and media only

Hibsago (bepirovirsen) approved in the US for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB)

- Approval based on phase III data showing unprecedented functional cure rates compared to standard of care

- Six-month treatment with option of self-administration after first dose

- CHB affects approximately 1.7 million people in the US1

GSK plc (LSE/NYSE: GSK) today announced that the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Hibsago (bepirovirsen) for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B (CHB) virus infection in combination with nucleos(t)ide analogue reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NrtI) therapy in adult patients without cirrhosis, receiving Nrtl therapy for at least 6 months, who have suppressed HBV deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA), and with hepatitis B virus (HBV) surface antigen (HBsAg) levels ≤3000 IU/ml, as determined by an FDA-authorised test.2 Bepirovirsen is a first in class antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) and offers unprecedented functional cure rates compared to current standard of care. The approval was granted under FDA priority review and Breakthrough Therapy Designation, recognising significant improvement of bepirovirsen and nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy over existing standard of care.3

Tony Wood, Chief Scientific Officer, GSK, said: “Despite current therapies, many people living with chronic hepatitis B remain on treatment indefinitely and continue to face the risk of serious liver complications.4,5 For the first time, with Hibsago, US patients have the potential to achieve functional cure after a six-month treatment course, with the added convenience of the option of self-administration after the first dose.”

The approval was supported by results from the B-WELL phase III trials showing functional cure rates of 19% in adults with ≤3000 IU/ml HBsAg, compared to current standard of care alone, which typically achieves less than 1% functional cure rate after one year of treatment.6,7 Functional cure occurs when HBV DNA and viral protein - HBsAg - are undetectable for at least 24 weeks after stopping all treatment, indicating the disease is controlled by the immune system without medication.8

Dr. Norah Terrault, Chief of Gastroenterology & Hepatology, USC Keck Medical Centre, said: “This is the start of a new era in treating people living with CHB. Bepirovirsen offers patients the potential to achieve functional cure after a short period of treatment, a long-standing goal for patients and physicians alike."

Dr. Chari Cohen, President of Hepatitis B Foundation, said: “CHB is a major public health challenge, affecting millions of people in the US and accounting for approximately 56% of all global liver cancer cases.1,9 Today marks significant progress towards our aim of transforming the way CHB is managed with improvements in screening, diagnosis, and the availability of innovative treatment options for our community.”

Quantitative surface antigen testing will support the diagnosis and identification of patients suitable for treatment with bepirovirsen who have baseline HBsAg levels ≤3000 IU/ml. Several tests are available, including a recently authorised FDA test.

GSK continues to advance regulatory submissions for bepirovirsen across multiple geographies with key regulatory decisions anticipated in the coming months.

Results from the B-Well phase III trials

Pooled data from the B-Well phase III trials showed that six-month treatment with bepirovirsen achieved a clinically meaningful 19% functional cure response rate (233 of 1,220 vs. 0 of 614 in the placebo group). B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 each met the primary end point, demonstrating a statistically significant improvement in functional cure versus placebo in the overall study population (adults with ≤3000 IU/ml HBsAg level). In a key secondary endpoint, a functional cure rate of 26% (200 of 768 vs. 0 of 393 in the placebo group) was achieved in participants with ≤1000 IU/ml HBsAg level, a group that represents approximately 45% of diagnosed CHB cases globally.10

Exploratory analyses also showed bepirovirsen reduced HBsAg to ≤100 IU/ml in 49% of participants (598 of 1220) in the overall study population, and in 62% of bepirovirsen recipients in the ≤1000 IU/ml (476 of 768) sub-group11 as of the week 72 visit. Medical literature has linked this low level of surface antigen with increased immune control and improved patient outcomes.12,13,14

The trials showed an acceptable safety and tolerability profile consistent with other studies of bepirovirsen. The three most frequently observed adverse events were injection site erythema, local pain and temporary rise in the blood level of a liver enzyme.

About bepirovirsen

Bepirovirsen is an antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designed to recognise and inhibit the production of the genetic components (i.e. RNA) of the hepatitis B virus that can lead to chronic disease, potentially allowing a person’s immune system to regain control. Bepirovirsen reduces the production of RNA and viral proteins associated with HBV, suppresses the level of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) in the blood, and may stimulate the immune system to increase the chances of a durable and sustained response.

GSK licensed bepirovirsen from Ionis Pharmaceuticals and collaborated with them on its development. Bepirovirsen has been recognised by global regulatory authorities for its innovation and potential to address significant unmet need in hepatitis B, with Breakthrough Designation and priority review from the US FDA, Breakthrough Therapy and Priority Review designation in China and SENKU designation in Japan. Bepirovirsen is approved in Japan and the US.

Please see accompanying US Prescribing Information here.

item.titleRaw: Antidepressants: new safety measures for all patients to improve communication of the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and persistent sexual dysfunction
item.titleZh: 英国MHRA对抗抑郁药实施新安全措施

cases.text:
Antidepressants: new safety measures for all patients to improve communication of the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and persistent sexual dysfunction

New safety measures are now being implemented to improve how the risks of suicidal thoughts and behaviours and persistent sexual dysfunction are communicated to patients taking antidepressant medications.

Summary

New safety measures are now being implemented for all patients taking antidepressant medications. This follows completion of a detailed review, involving patients and their families, into how the risks of suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and persistent sexual dysfunction are communicated in the patient information leaflets (PILs) that accompany antidepressant medications. These changes involve a new boxed warning in the PIL, a new patient card, and a supporting safety (ancillary) leaflet. The term post SSRI sexual dysfunction (“PSSD”) is also being added to the PIL for some antidepressant medications.

Advice for Healthcare Professionals:

- discuss with patients when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant or at their next review, the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours. Advise patients to seek urgent medical attention if they experience new or worsening feelings of suicidal intent in relation to starting an antidepressant, especially early in treatment or following dose changes

- discuss with patients when starting or changing the dose of an antidepressant, or at their next review, that there is evidence that some antidepressants[footnote 1]. are associated with a risk of sexual dysfunction and that symptoms may continue after stopping treatment with certain antidepressants. Some patients refer to this as “PSSD”

- follow the relevant NICE guidance[footnote 2]. and monitor your patients regularly after starting treatment with an antidepressant

- give your patient the safety (ancillary) leaflet when it becomes available in 2027 to support your risks and benefits discussions

- report suspected adverse reactions associated with antidepressants on a Yellow Card

Advice for Healthcare Professionals to Provide to Patients:

- if you have new or worsening suicidal thoughts, particularly when starting or changing dose of antidepressants, seek urgent medical attention. You can call NHS 111, or your local mental health crisis team, Samaritans on 116 123, or text “SHOUT” to 85258. You can find more information and support options on the NHS website

- there is the potential for you to experience sexual dysfunction with some antidepressants, which may continue even after you stop the medicine. Please contact your healthcare professional if you have any concerns

- these are not new risks for these medicines, but it is important to be aware of them

- do not stop taking your medicine without first speaking to your healthcare professional

- please also read the patient card and the Patient Information Leaflet which contains important information about your medicine

- when it becomes available in 2027, you will also receive a supporting safety (ancillary) leaflet explaining the benefits and risks of treatment options to help you have informed discussions with your healthcare professional about taking your medicine safely

- report suspected side effects via the Yellow Card scheme

Background

A Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) Expert Working Group (EWG) on the effectiveness of antidepressant risk minimisation measures was convened in response to concerns raised by patients and their families about whether patient information leaflets (PILs) adequately communicate the risks of suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and sexual dysfunction where symptoms may continue after stopping treatment. The EWG met between May 2024 and July 2025 and their recommendations were considered by the CHM in September 2025.

Central to the considerations of the EWG were the views of patients and families about the effectiveness of warnings in the current antidepressants’ PILs. The EWG considered the views in the context of the literature published since 2019, when the regulatory position on suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and sexual dysfunction where symptoms continued were last reviewed at a committee level.

The EWG heard directly from the families of some patients and from individual patients who shared their experiences and suggestions for improvements to safety messaging.

The EWG considered the patients’ and families’ views on the need for additional measures to raise awareness of warnings about the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and sexual dysfunction where symptoms may continue after stopping treatment. They made recommendations to the CHM on regulatory options.

The CHM advised that updates to strengthen the wording on the risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviours in the PILs should be developed through user testing with patients representing a range of mental health conditions. The MHRA subsequently worked with the Patients Association, who brought together a focus group of patients to provide further feedback, to refine and finalise the updated wording and format of the PILs.

New measures

The Commission on Human Medicines (CHM) has advised the MHRA on several regulatory actions and the need for consistent safety messaging across the healthcare system. These include:

- A new boxed warning in the PILs to better highlight information on suicidal thoughts and behaviours, and signpost to where patients can get help.

- A new patient card available in digital or hard copy formats to reinforce key safety messages. The expectation is that the hard copy card will be designed to be credit card sized and easy for patients to carry. Initially the card will be available electronically and may be given to the patient by dispensers as an interim measure ahead of cards becoming available. cases.text:
以下受影响产品及针对这些设备的处理建议未发生变化。本次召回涉及更新设备使用说明，不涉及将设备从使用或销售场所移除。美国食品药品监督管理局已将本次召回确定为最严重级别。若您继续在不遵循更新后说明的情况下使用该设备，可能导致严重伤害或死亡。受影响产品 图1：Lumify换能器 图2：Lumify换能器连接至兼容的Android设备或iOS设备 美国食品药品监督管理局已知悉Philips Ultrasound已向受影响客户发出信函，建议所有Lumify诊断超声系统更新使用说明。受影响设备：软件版本 UDI-DI（GTIN） Lumify诊断超声系统 iOS（2.X）00884838103405 Lumify诊断超声系统 iOS（5.0）00884838120266 Lumify诊断超声系统 iOS（5.1.2）00884838124141 Lumify诊断超声系统 iOS（5.1.3）00884838124141 Lumify诊断超声系统 Android（1.X）00884838106987 Lumify诊断超声系统 Android（3.X）00884838100121 Lumify诊断超声系统 Android（4.X）00884838108455 Lumify诊断超声系统 Android（5.1）00884838122116 Lumify诊断超声系统 Android（5.1.1）00884838122116 应采取的措施 为防止扫描功能意外丢失或延迟，除非可立即获得备用超声设备，否则仅在Wi-Fi/蜂窝信号易于获取的区域使用Lumify诊断超声系统。2026年9月24日，Philips Ultrasound向所有受影响客户发出信函，建议采取以下措施：为防止扫描功能意外丢失或延迟，除非可立即获得备用超声设备，否则仅在Wi-Fi/蜂窝信号易于获取的区域使用Lumify诊断超声系统。始终备有备用超声设备和/或检查手段以供诊疗使用。

将 Philips Ultrasound 提供的信函传达给该设备的所有使用者，使其了解该产品问题及相关危害/伤害。将 Philips Ultrasound 提供的通知张贴在受影响设备附近，以便查阅。纠正原因 Philips Ultrasound 表示，由于软件问题，与其超声换能器配合使用的 Lumify Android 或 iOS 应用程序可能无法识别先前已注册的换能器，并会在床旁使用前无预警地提示用户重新注册。在完成注册步骤之前，扫描功能将被阻止。注册需要 Wi-Fi 或蜂窝信号接入。在医院外使用的 Lumify 设备（例如在救护车、飞机或现场环境中）由于 Wi-Fi/蜂窝信号接入更为有限，风险更高。Philips 已收到报告称，意外的重新注册事件已导致在院前环境中无法进行扫描，并延误了患者救治。这些院前事件发生在 Wi-Fi 或蜂窝信号接入范围之外。Philips 表示正在开发软件更新以解决注册问题。一旦软件更新可用，Philips 将发送后续通知，并就所需采取的任何措施提供说明。此外，Philips 报告称，Lumify 换能器 USB 线缆与客户平板电脑或手机之间的连接在使用过程中可能断开或连接不稳定，这可能中断设备的持续运行并导致救治延误。Philips 表示正在评估连接问题的原因并确定适当的解决方案。一旦获得进一步信息，将尽快向客户通报更新。操作过程中功能丧失或系统故障可能导致诊断和/或治疗延误。

由于 Lumify 系统旨在用于床旁即时使用，即超声成像支持快速诊断与治疗、实时决策、不稳定患者的分诊，以及在移动、医疗资源不足或偏远环境中获得诊断能力，因此其功能丧失或系统故障可能比传统超声设备造成更严重的后果。根据临床情况和患者状况，诊断或治疗的延迟可能导致严重伤害或死亡。截至 2026 年 9 月 29 日，Philips Ultrasound 已报告与该问题相关的 8 例严重伤害和 4 例死亡。器械用途 Philips Lumify 超声系统由 Philips 换能器、Philips Lumify 应用程序以及兼容的 Android 设备或兼容的 iOS 设备组合而成。其适应证为诊断性超声成像和流体流动分析。Lumify 系统旨在用于提供医疗保健的环境。该器械可运输，并可在医院以外的场所使用，例如救护车内。联系信息 美国境内出现不良反应、质量问题或对该问题有疑问的客户，应联系 Philips Ultrasound 客户关怀解决方案中心，电话 (800) 722-9377。其他 FDA 资源 FDA 执法报告 CDRH 医疗器械召回数据库 唯一器械标识（UDI） 唯一器械标识（UDI）有助于识别在美国销售的单个医疗器械，从分销到使用全程可追溯。UDI 使不良事件报告能够更准确地报告、审查和分析，从而可以更快地识别器械，并因此可能更快地解决问题。我如何在标签上识别 UDI？AccessGUDID 数据库 - 识别您的医疗器械 UDI 系统的优势 我如何报告问题？

item.titleRaw: 国家药监局关于修订降脂灵制剂和乳块消口服制剂说明书的公告（2026年第102号）
item.titleZh: 国家药监局关于修订降脂灵制剂和乳块消口服制剂说明书的公告（2026年第102号）

cases.text:
根据药品不良反应评估结果，为进一步保障公众用药安全，国家药品监督管理局决定对降脂灵制剂（片、分散片、颗粒）和乳块消口服制剂（片、颗粒、胶囊、软胶囊、丸、口服液和糖浆）说明书中的【警示语】、【不良反应】、【禁忌】和【注意事项】等进行统一修订。现将有关事项公告如下：

一、所有上述药品的上市许可持有人均应当依据《药品注册管理办法》等有关规定，按照要求修订说明书（见附件1、2），于2027年1月18日前报省级药品监督管理部门备案。

修订内容涉及药品标签的，应当一并进行修订；说明书及标签其他内容应当与原批准内容一致。在备案之日起生产的药品，不得继续使用原药品说明书。药品上市许可持有人应当在备案后9个月内对已出厂的药品说明书及标签予以更换，或者以其他适当形式将更新信息告知患者。

二、药品上市许可持有人应当对新增不良反应发生机制开展深入研究，采取有效措施做好药品使用和安全性问题的宣传培训，指导医师、药师或者患者合理用药。

三、临床医师、药师应当仔细阅读上述药品说明书的修订内容，在选择用药时，应当根据新修订说明书进行充分的获益/风险分析。

四、患者用药前应当仔细阅读药品说明书，使用处方药的，应当严格遵医嘱用药。

五、省级药品监督管理部门应当督促行政区域内上述药品的上市许可持有人按要求做好相应说明书修订和标签、说明书更换及说明书更新信息的告知工作，对违法违规行为依法严厉查处。

特此公告。

item.titleRaw: 12.75亿美元首付！吉利德买断瀚辰星泰环肽
item.titleZh: 12.75亿美元首付！吉利德买断瀚辰星泰环肽

cases.text:
2026年10月23日，吉利德科学宣布与瀚辰星泰（PepStar Therapeutics）达成最终协议，拟以12.75亿美元现金首付款收购其口服IL-23R抑制剂项目，核心资产为处于I期临床的HCXT-2001，交易预计2026年第四季度完成，吉利德获得全球权益。

值得注意的是，这不是近年国产创新药常见的授权许可，而是直接把项目买断。考虑到HCXT-2001仍处早期测试、尚无已发表临床数据，这一预付款金额引人注目。

从技术看，HCXT-2001属于口服大环肽路线，试图兼顾小分子的口服便利性与抗体级别的蛋白结合能力、强结合力，半衰期延长，为口服抑制IL-23通路提供差异化方案。

吉利德的算盘也较清晰。这笔收购发生在其口服炎症性肠病（IBD）在研药emvistegrast公布积极中期结果之后，可为其IBD组合再添一员，并可能单独或联合开发，帮助公司摆脱对核心HIV业务的单一依赖。

IL‑23受体是免疫介导性炎症疾病领域已得到临床验证的关键靶点，在斑块状银屑病、银屑病关节炎、炎症性肠病的发病通路中发挥核心作用。

目前，由强生与Protagonist联合开发的全球首创口服 IL‑23R 拮抗剂icotrokinra，已于2026年3月获得美国FDA批准，用于中重度斑块状银屑病，给药方案为每日一次口服。

炎症性肠病属于需要长期持续管理的慢病，在这条赛道上，给药间隔的长效化设计，有望成为拉开产品差异化竞争力的关键变量。翰森制药的 HS‑20118（AVR‑001）在Ib期银屑病研究中，展现出支持每周一次口服给药的潜力；该资产通过对外授权给 Avere，并依托Avere与NextCure合并组建NewCo的模式完成出海，交易包含1.2亿美元首付款，最高里程碑金额可达21.8亿美元。与此同时，海思科也在布局同靶点口服肽管线，借助双环肽、环化改造等技术方向探索差异化成药路径。

item.titleRaw: EQT to Acquire Qiagen for $12.1B, Plans to Take Tools, Diagnostics Provider Private
item.titleZh: EQT 以 121 亿美元收购 Qiagen 并将其私有化

cases.text: An entity of Swedish private equity firm EQT has agreed to acquire Qiagen for €10.8 billion (about $12.1 billion) cash, both said today, in a deal that would take private the global life-sciences tools, diagnostics, and workflow solutions provider following on-and-off takeover attempts over nearly seven years. The buyer is EQT Private Equity, a holding company indirectly controlled by the firm’s EQT XI fund and managed and controlled by affiliates of EQT. Within EQT Private Equity, “indirect participations” or stakes are held by co-investors Luxinva, a wholly owned subsidiary of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority; and CPP Investment Board Europe, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Canada Pension Plan Investment Board or CPP Investments. EQT’s takeover offer followed what Qiagen called a comprehensive review by its Supervisory Board and Managing Board evaluating the company’s strategic prospects through discussions with strategic and financial parties. Qiagen said that its boards concluded that a buyout by EQT would offer the best prospects for the company’s next growth phase by giving it greater flexibility to invest longer term under a private owner while providing shareholders with attractive and certain cash value. “After considering Qiagen’s stand-alone strategic prospects and the alternatives available through discussions with strategic and financial parties, we unanimously concluded that this is the best path forward for Qiagen, its shareholders, and other stakeholders,” Stephen H. Rusckowski, chairman of Qiagen’s Supervisory Board, said in a statement. ‘Compelling value’ “This transaction offers shareholders compelling value while positioning Qiagen for its next phase of development under private ownership,” Rusckowski added. News of Qiagen’s strategic review emerged in January through a Bloomberg News report that said the company was weighing a potential sale, attributed to unnamed sources, amid fresh interest from would-be buyers in acquiring the company. Investors reacted to news of the strategic review with a buying surge that sent Qiagen shares to their highest levels since February 2023, a 17% one-week gain that saw its New York Stock Exchange shares rise from $47.57 on January 16 to $55.62 on January 23. Qiagen’s European shares, traded on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange’s XETRA market, rose 12.5% from €40.99 ($45.55) to €46.13 ($51.46). Qiagen shares slipped since then as investors questioned whether the company would reach agreement with a buyer, and as the company lowered its full-year guidance to investors. In April, Qiagen cut its net sales growth forecast from 5% down to 1–2%, while lowering its adjusted diluted EPS forecast from $2.50 to $2.43. The reductions followed weaker than anticipated sales—a year-over-year 5% drop at constant exchange rates—of Qiagen’s QuantiFERON blood test kit due to reduced demand for immigration-related tuberculosis testing in the U.S. and Middle East. Qiagen shares reached a 52-week low of €27.56 ($30.62) May 12 on XETRA and $32.13 the following day on NYSE before climbing back to the low €40s on XETRA and mid-$40s on NYSE. Cautious investor reaction On Thursday, investors appeared to react cautiously to the deal. Shares on XETRA rose 5% from €42.82 ($47.77) to € 44.94 ($50.13). On NYSE, shares barely rose 0.4%, from an even $50 to $50.22. Qiagen has suspended its full-year guidance for this year due to the planned acquisition. At €46.50 ($51.88) per share, EQT Equity Partners’ offer for Qiagen represents an 8.6% premium above Qiagen’s closing stock price Wednesday—but a premium of 40.3% to the XETRA closing price of €33.15 ($36.84) on July 8, the last trading day before news reports about private equity firms being interested in acquiring Qiagen. The premium climbs to 46.9% when compared to the three-month volume-weighted average price (VWAP) on XETRA of €31.66 ($35.18) per Qiagen share up to and including July 8. The €10.8 billion ($12.1 billion) enterprise value of the deal includes approximately $1.1 billion of net debt, Qiagen said. “Qiagen’s management team and employees have built an exceptional company with a portfolio of highly attractive products and respected brands, strong market positions and considerable technical expertise,” stated Matteo Thun-Hohenstein, Partner at EQT. “EQT brings deep sector experience, a global network and operational capabilities, and we are proud to partner with Qiagen’s highly talented and capable employees to further invest in Qiagen’s continued product innovation and growth.” Track record EQT has €354 billion in assets under management and a three-decade track record of acquiring, developing, and sometimes selling companies that include life sciences tools/tech concerns. In 2019, EQT acquired a majority interest in Aldevron , which it sold two years later to Danaher for approximately $9.6 billion. Also in 2021, EQT joined the private equity business of Goldman Sachs to acquire contract research organization Parexel for $8.5 billion . In 2023, EQT co-led a €129 million ($138 million at the time; $144 million today) Series A financing of Amsterdam biotech VectorY , with proceeds intended toward advancing its vectorized antibodies for neurodegenerative disease treatment. Other current and former portfolio companies of EQT include SPT Labtech, Galderma, Dako and HemoCue. EQT says its healthcare and life sciences experience includes around 100 investment professionals across 15 countries, with over €30 billion (about $33.6 billion) invested across more than 210 companies in healthcare globally. EQT Private Equity said it had obtained enough committed equity and debt financing to fund the offer and related transaction costs. Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, Deutsche Bank, SMBC, Crédit Agricole, and UniCredit are acting as bookrunners and mandated lead arrangers for the committed debt financing. item.titleRaw: AbbVie Announces Topline Results from the Phase 3 INTREPID Trial Showing Lutikizumab Significantly Improved Signs and Symptoms of Disease in Patients with Hidradenitis Suppurativa
item.titleZh: Lutikizumab 3期INTREPID研究达到主要终点

cases.text:
October 22, 2026

AbbVie Announces Topline Results from the Phase 3 INTREPID Trial Showing Lutikizumab Significantly Improved Signs and Symptoms of Disease in Patients with Hidradenitis Suppurativa

- In the Phase 3 INTREPID study, lutikizumab achieved the primary endpoint of Hidradenitis Suppurativa Clinical Response 75 (HiSCR75) at Week 16 compared with placebo1

- Lutikizumab met 8 ranked secondary endpoints, including significant improvements in HS-related skin pain at Week 8 and significant reductions in the occurrence of HS flares over the first 16 weeks,1 reflecting outcomes assessed by both patients and physicians

- Lutikizumab was generally well tolerated, with no new safety concerns identified1

- INTREPID provides Phase 3 data supporting the continued investigation of simultaneous inhibition of IL-1α and IL-1β as a potential treatment approach in adults and adolescents with moderate to severe HS1

NORTH CHICAGO, Ill., Oct. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- AbbVie (NYSE: ABBV) today announced positive topline results from the Phase 3 INTREPID study evaluating the safety and efficacy of lutikizumab, an investigational dual-variable-domain interleukin (IL) 1α/1β antagonist, in adults and adolescents with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa (HS). The study met its primary endpoint and 8 ranked secondary endpoints.

In the INTREPID study, patients treated with lutikizumab achieved significantly higher response rates for the primary endpoint of HiSCR75 at Week 16 compared with placebo (31.4% versus 23.4%; p≤0.001). HiSCR75 is defined as at least a 75% reduction from baseline in the total abscess and inflammatory nodule (AN) count, with no increase in abscess count and no increase in draining fistula count relative to baseline. INTREPID is the first phase 3 study including adults and adolescents with HS to demonstrate statistically significant HiSCR75 response rates at Week 16 as the primary endpoint.

Lutikizumab also demonstrated statistically significant improvements across key ranked secondary endpoints, including rapid reductions in HS-related pain and significantly fewer HS flares, compared to placebo. At Week 8, 26.2% of patients treated with lutikizumab achieved NRS3, defined as at least a 3-point reduction from baseline in HS-related skin pain on the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS), compared with 15.0% of patients receiving placebo (p<0.0001). Improvements in NRS3 were reported as early as Week 1. In addition, at Week 8, 36.0% of patients receiving lutikizumab achieved NRS30, defined as at least a 30% reduction and at least a 2-unit reduction from baseline in HS-related skin pain, compared with 22.8% of patients receiving placebo (p<0.0001). Lutikizumab also significantly reduced the occurrence of HS flares during the first 16 weeks compared with placebo (18.4% versus 28.1% patients experienced flares; p<0.0001).1

Additional improvements were observed in quality-of-life measures, including changes from baseline in the dermatology life quality index (DLQI) and hidradenitis suppurativa impact assessment (HSIA) (p<0.0001 for each). Key potential disease drivers, including IL-17A and IL-17F levels were also reduced over the double-blind 16-week treatment period. These findings reinforce the potential for lutikizumab to address the burden of disease for people living with moderate to severe HS.

"Elevated levels of IL-1α and IL-1β have been identified in HS lesions, supporting the mechanistic rationale for evaluating lutikizumab in HS. These results further validate our science-led approach and demonstrate how AbbVie applies its deep immunology expertise in our efforts to advance potentially differentiated new treatments grounded in disease biology," said Kori Wallace, M.D., vice president, global head of immunology clinical development, AbbVie. "In addition to achieving the rigorous bar set by HiSCR75, lutikizumab also significantly improved HS-related skin pain and disease flares, reinforcing the importance of an approach to HS that addresses outcomes assessed by both physicians and most importantly, patients."

The safety profile of lutikizumab was similar to prior studies, with no new safety concerns identified. Overall, treatment-emergent adverse event (TEAE) rates were similar with lutikizumab and placebo: any adverse event (AE) (53.4% vs 53.7%), any serious AE (3.0% vs 2.9%), and AEs leading to discontinuation (1.7% vs 1.9%), respectively. The most frequently reported TEAEs associated with lutikizumab (≥ 3%) were nasopharyngitis, upper respiratory tract infections, headache, fatigue, and injection-site reactions. With the exception of injection-site reactions, their rates were similar to placebo. Similar rates of oral candidiasis were also observed between the lutikizumab and placebo groups (0.3% vs 0.4%, respectively). There was no suicidal ideation observed in either the lutikizumab or placebo group. There were no deaths in the lutikizumab group; one death occurred in the placebo group.

"Hidradenitis suppurativa remains an underserved disease and many patients continue to struggle with pain and disease flares despite available therapies," said Alexa B. Kimball, M.D., M.P.H., President and CEO of Harvard Medical Faculty Physicians at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center, Boston, and Professor of Dermatology at Harvard Medical School. "The INTREPID data are notable because the primary endpoint of HiSCR75 sets a rigorous bar for defining clinical response. These are also the first Phase 3 data evaluating the effect of targeting both IL-1α and IL-1β on this disease. Taken together, these results underscore the promising potential of this investigational treatment."

These data will be presented at a future medical congress. Additional data from the Phase 3 INTREPID study, including results from a 36-week blinded extension period, are expected in 2027 and will be used to support regulatory submissions for lutikizumab in hidradenitis suppurativa in the second half of the year.

cases.text:
- Third-quarter reported sales growth of 14.5 percent; comparable sales growth of 7.0 percent

- Third-quarter GAAP diluted EPS of $0.53; adjusted diluted EPS of $1.42

- Expands portfolio with key new product approvals

ABBOTT PARK, Ill., Oct. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Abbott (NYSE: ABT) today announced financial results for the third quarter ended Sept. 30, 2026.

- Third-quarter sales increased 14.5 percent on a reported basis and 7.0 percent on a comparable basis.

- Third-quarter GAAP diluted EPS of $0.53 and adjusted diluted EPS of $1.42, which excludes specified items.

- Abbott projects full-year 2026 comparable sales growth to be approximately 6.0 percent1.

- Abbott reaffirms the midpoint of previously provided full-year 2026 adjusted diluted EPS guidance range and tightens the range to $5.50 to $5.55.

- In August, Abbott announced U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval for Libre® Duo, the world's first dual glucose-ketone biowearable sensor. By providing real-time visibility into glucose and ketone levels, this new technology helps optimize the management of diabetes by detecting rising ketone levels, which can lead to diabetic ketoacidosis, a serious health condition for people with diabetes.

- In August, Abbott announced that the company received CE Mark for its Amulet 360™ Left Atrial Appendage (LAA) Occluder, a next-generation device designed to reduce the risk of stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation (AFib).

- In August, Abbott announced the launch of Similac® 360 Total Care® Made With Whole Milk — the first and only commercially sterile, ready-to-feed liquid infant formula made with whole milk in the United States.

- In September, Abbott announced FDA approval for its TactiFlex™ Duo Ablation Catheter, Sensor Enabled™, designed to deliver both pulsed field ablation (PFA) and radiofrequency (RF) energy to treat patients battling atrial fibrillation.

- In September, Abbott launched SimpleScreen™ CRC, an FDA-approved, blood-based colorectal cancer screening test for adults age 45 and older who are at average risk for the disease.

"Abbott delivered strong third-quarter results, reflecting balanced growth across our portfolio," said Robert B. Ford, chairman and chief executive officer, Abbott. "With strong performance across multiple businesses and a robust pipeline of innovation, we are well-positioned to deliver sustainable growth in the years ahead."

Management believes that measuring sales growth on a comparable basis is an appropriate way for investors to best understand the underlying performance of the business. Comparable sales growth includes the prior and current year sales of Exact Sciences, a cancer diagnostics company that Abbott acquired on March 23, 2026. Comparable sales growth excludes the impact of foreign exchange and revenue in both the prior and current year related to compensation payments that Abbott's Structural Heart business received as part of a multi-year agreement with a competitor. The final payment under this agreement was recognized in the first quarter of 2026.

item.titleRaw: 刚刚！樊英教授：国产HER2 ADC头对头击败化疗｜2026ESMO
item.titleZh: 刚刚！樊英教授：国产HER2 ADC头对头击败化疗｜2026ESMO

cases.text:
*仅供医学专业人士阅读参考

HER2低表达乳腺癌PFS翻倍

整理 | 高楼

2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）年会于10月23日至27日在西班牙马德里盛大召开，一批由中国学者牵头的重磅研究将在会上集中亮相。医学界推出"刚刚"系列，聚焦ESMO会议大事件，把握肿瘤治疗脉搏。在这里，我们跨越时差，触摸前沿。

就在刚刚！西班牙时间10月23日13时40分（北京时间19时40分），中国医学科学院肿瘤医院樊英教授在早期与晚期乳腺癌专场汇报了突破性摘要LBA13——HORIZON-Breast06研究，该研究评估瑞康曲妥珠单抗（SHR-A1811）治疗HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌的疗效与安全性，结果同步发表于JAMA。医学界特此整理，以飨读者。

图1：樊英教授在ESMO2026年会大会现场汇报

被重新定义的庞大人群，化疗后几无退路

HER2低表达指免疫组化（IHC）1+，或IHC 2+且原位杂交（ISH）阴性。据介绍，乳腺癌中HER2低表达占45%~55%，构成了乳腺癌中最大的一个群体。然而，这类患者在传统治疗下获益有限。

瑞康曲妥珠单抗（SHR-A1811）是靶向HER2的抗体偶联药物（ADC），由曲妥珠单抗、可切割四肽连接子与拓扑异构酶Ⅰ抑制剂载荷偶联而成。HORIZON-Breast06即为评估该药用于HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌的III期研究。

共同主要终点，551例随机对照

研究入组经中心确认的HER2低表达转移性乳腺癌患者，要求转移阶段既往化疗≤1线。受试者按1:1随机接受瑞康曲妥珠单抗6.4 mg/kg静脉输注、每3周一次，或研究者选择化疗（紫杉类、艾立布林、卡培他滨或吉西他滨）。

双共同主要终点为盲法独立中心审查（BICR）评估的初治及总体人群无进展生存期（PFS）；

关键次要终点包括总体及化疗初治人群总生存期（OS）、化疗经治人群PFS

2023年6月30日至2025年8月20日，共730例患者接受筛选，179例排除后，551例完成随机分组——瑞康曲妥珠单抗组277例、化疗组274例，分别有276例与271例接受治疗。数据截止日期为2026年3月20日，中位随访18.0个月（95%CI 16.8~19.3）；至截止时，两组仍在治疗者分别为102例与22例。

基线特征上，化疗初治者占81.5%，HR阳性者占73.0%，既往接受CDK4/6抑制剂治疗者占64.8%。其中HR阳性人群两组各201例，HR阴性人群分别为76例与73例，两组基线均衡。

中位PFS翻倍，进展风险降七成

化疗初治人群中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组中位PFS为16.6个月（95%CI 14.0~19.4），化疗组为6.8个月（95%CI 5.7~7.0），疾病进展或死亡风险降低75%（HR 0.25，95%CI 0.19~0.33，P<0.001）。

图2：初治人群PFS生存曲线

总体人群中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组中位PFS为16.4个月（95%CI 14.0~16.8），化疗组为6.8个月（95%CI 5.7~6.9），风险降低73%（HR 0.27，95%CI 0.21~0.34，P<0.001）；PFS事件数分别为130例（46.9%）与185例（67.5%）。两个共同主要终点均达成。

在既往接受过化疗的人群中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组中位PFS为13.9个月（95%CI 9.7~16.6），化疗组为5.6个月（95%CI 4.0~8.4），风险降低68%（HR 0.32，95%CI 0.19~0.54）。

亚组全线一致，HR阴性人群同获显著改善

1. 预设亚组分析显示，PFS获益在各人群中保持一致，各亚组的风险比均显著小于1：

HR阳性人群中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组中位PFS为16.4个月、化疗组为6.7个月（HR 0.24）；HR阴性人群中，分别为18.5个月与6.8个月（HR 0.34）。

在HR阴性人群中，按PD-L1状态分层后优势依然明确：PD-L1阳性者的ORR为95.2% vs 42.9%；PD-L1阴性或未知者为70.9% vs 42.3%。

图3：亚组分析：HR阳性/阴性人群PFS生存曲线

2. 客观缓解率（ORR）方面：

化疗初治人群中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组为76.0%、化疗组为43.3%；

化疗经治人群中，分别为73.1%与32.0%；

总体人群中，分别为75.5%与41.2%。

临床获益率与中位缓解持续时间同样以瑞康曲妥珠单抗组更优。

3. OS数据尚不成熟，目前为描述性分析，已观察到143例OS事件，研究计划后续进行中期与最终分析。

在总体人群中，12个月OS率分别为90.6%与81.4%，死亡风险降低33%（HR 0.67，95%CI 0.48~0.94）；

在化疗初治人群中，12个月OS率分别为92.0%与83.0%，死亡风险降低38%（HR 0.62，95%CI 0.41~0.93）。

安全性可管理，ILD发生率仅2.5%

安全性分析中，瑞康曲妥珠单抗组276例、化疗组271例，中位治疗持续时间分别为13.8个月（95%CI 11.9~16.3）与5.6个月（95%CI 4.6~6.0）。≥3级治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）发生率分别为84.1%与67.9%。

发生率超过20%的TRAE中，贫血发生率在瑞康曲妥珠单抗组为92.8%（≥3级42.8%），化疗组为59.0%（≥3级4.8%）；白细胞计数降低分别为88.4%（≥3级56.5%）与84.5%（≥3级35.4%）；此外还包括中性粒细胞计数降低、恶心、脱发、疲劳等，以血液学毒性为主。间质性肺病（ILD）是HER2 ADC最受关注的安全性事件，本研究中瑞康曲妥珠单抗组仅7例（2.5%）报告。

图4：治疗相关不良事件

研究结论

与化疗相比，瑞康曲妥珠单抗在PFS上显示出优效性；在HR阴性、HR阳性等预设亚组中，PFS获益保持一致；安全性可控，ILD发生率低。

item.titleRaw: 王树森教授：中位PFS达16.4个月！TQB2102治疗HER2低表达乳腺癌Ⅲ期结果出炉｜2026 ESMO
item.titleZh: 王树森教授：中位PFS达16.4个月！TQB2102治疗HER2低表达乳腺癌Ⅲ期结果出炉｜2026 ESMO

cases.text:
*仅供医学专业人士阅读参考

整理：书池

2026年10月23日至27日，由欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）主办的2026年欧洲肿瘤内科学会年会在西班牙马德里举办。23日，中山大学肿瘤防治中心王树森教授报告了随机III期APEX-Breast01研究（LBA27）结果。

该研究聚焦既往未接受过晚期化疗的HER2低表达复发或转移性乳腺癌（r/m BC）患者，旨在比较双表位HER2靶向抗体偶联药物（ADC）TQB2102与研究者选择化疗（TPC）的疗效与安全性差异，为HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌后线治疗决策提供重要循证证据。

图1 王树森教授汇报

TQB2102vs研究者选择化疗：HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌后线的策略对比

▌研究设计与入组人群

APEX-Breast01是一项随机、对照的III期确证性研究，纳入既往未接受过晚期化疗的HER2低表达复发或转移性乳腺癌患者，包括转移性疾病阶段内分泌治疗进展后的HR+患者，及CPS<1或状态未知的HR-患者。

患者按1:1随机分组，分别接受TQB2102（7.5mg/kg，每3周一次）或研究者选择化疗（TPC：卡培他滨、紫杉醇或白蛋白紫杉醇）。

▌研究终点

主要终点为独立评审委员会（BIRC）评估的HR+/HER2低表达患者无进展生存期（PFS），关键次要终点为全部HER2低表达患者的PFS。

▌基线资料与研究实施情况

截至2026年5月31日，共543例患者随机分组（TQB2102组269例、TPC组274例），其中HR+患者461例（占84.9%，该亚组91.3%既往接受过CDK4/6抑制剂）、HR−患者约82例。两组基线特征均衡：IHC 1+占比58.3% vs 57.9%，既往接受过紫杉类治疗62.3% vs 61.8%。

TQB2102组PFS显著占优，全人群获益一致

▌PFS

在HR+/HER2低表达人群中，TQB2102组中位PFS达16.4个月、化疗组仅5.5个月，风险比（HR）0.29（P<0.0001），疾病进展风险下降71%，中位PFS绝对延长10.9个月。全部HER2低表达人群结果几乎一致：16.4个月 vs 5.5个月，HR同为0.29（P<0.0001）。

图2 PFS(BIRC)：HR+/HER2-低表达主要终点

图3 PFS(BIRC)：全部HR+/HER2-低表达关键次要终点

▌客观缓解率（ORR）

TQB2102组ORR在HR+、全部HER2低表达及HR-人群中分别达66.7%、68.8%、80.5%，化疗组仅31.3%、31.0%、29.3%，其中HR+与全人群约为化疗组的2.1-2.2倍，HR-亚组达2.75倍、接近3倍。

图4 BIRC评估的ORR、CBR及DoR

▌安全性

在治疗相关不良事件（TRAE）方面，TQB2102安全性以血液学毒性为主，最常见的≥3级TRAE为中性粒细胞减少（30.1% vs 23.3%）和白细胞降低（21.6% vs 14.0%）。≥3级TRAE发生率为69.1% vs 42.4%。因TRAE停药比例两组均为1.5%（各4例），减量比例为34.2% vs 18.5%。TQB2102相关间质性肺病6例（2.2%，其中3级1.1%），整体可控。

图5 总体安全性数据

小结

该研究数据表明，TQB2102有望成为既往未化疗的HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌后线治疗的新选择，HR+与HR-人群一致获益进一步拓宽了适用人群。长期以来，HER2低表达晚期乳腺癌后线治疗依赖传统化疗，疗效与精准性皆受限，这项III期阳性结果有望打破临床僵局。展望未来，随着HER2靶向ADC机制的持续深耕与治疗线序前移，个体化、精准化的后线治疗策略有望重塑HER2低表达乳腺癌全程治疗格局，让更多患者获得更长的生存与更高的生活质量。

参考文献：

[1] Shusen Wang, et al. TQB2102 versus chemotherapy in HER2-low recurrent or metastatic breast cancer (r/m BC): Results from a randomized phase 3 study (APEX-Breast01). 2026 ESMO.

cases.text:
- OptimUM-01 and OptimUM-02 data supports the broad potential of darovasertib plus crizotinib to drive meaningful clinical benefits for patients with metastatic uveal melanoma, irrespective of HLA-A*02:01 allele status or line of therapy

- OptimUM-01 data demonstrates encouraging clinical activity from darovasertib combined with crizotinib in both treatment-naïve (7.4 month PFS, 27.1 month mOS, n=13) and heavily pretreated HLA-A*02:01-positive metastatic uveal melanoma, including in 2L patients following tebentafusp

- Treatment-naïve patients in OptimUM-01 and OptimUM-02 demonstrate comparable ORR, PFS and DOR in HLA-A*02:01-positive and -negative patients and consistent improvements in ORR and PFS versus investigator's choice of therapy across a range of clinically relevant subgroups

- OptimUM-09 continues to demonstrate robust tumor shrinkage in >80% of primary uveal melanoma patients treated with neoadjuvant darovasertib, resulting in a 57% eye preservation rate and 66% of patients achieving a reduced projected dose of radiation to critical eye structures in the enucleation and plaque brachytherapy cohorts, respectively

SOUTH SAN FRANCISCO, Calif., Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IDEAYA Biosciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: IDYA), a leading precision medicine oncology company, today announced updated clinical data from three ongoing studies evaluating darovasertib in metastatic and primary uveal melanoma (UM) that will be presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026, taking place on October 23–27 in Madrid, Spain. The updates will include Phase 2 expansion data from OptimUM-01 in HLA-A*02:01-positive patients with metastatic uveal melanoma (mUM), subgroup analyses from the registrational Phase 2/3 OptimUM-02 trial in first line (1L) HLA-A*02:01-negative mUM and follow-up data from the Phase 2 OptimUM-09 trial evaluating neoadjuvant darovasertib in patients with primary UM.

"These three clinical updates at ESMO continue to support our belief in the potential for darovasertib to address important unmet needs across the uveal melanoma treatment journey," said Yujiro S. Hata, Chief Executive Officer of IDEAYA Biosciences. "In the metastatic setting we believe the data from OptimUM-01 and OptimUM-02 offer strong and consistent evidence for the potential of darovasertib to address the needs of a broad patient population, irrespective of HLA-allele status. In primary disease, longer follow up data from OptimUM-09 continues to highlight the potential of neoadjuvant darovasertib to shrink tumors before primary local treatment to help more patients preserve their eyes and avoid the risk of long-term vision loss. Together, these data advance our vision of establishing darovasertib as a foundational therapy for uveal melanoma."

OptimUM-01 Activity in HLA-A*02:01-Positive Metastatic Uveal Melanoma

OptimUM-01 is a Phase 1/2 single-arm, multi-center, open label dose escalation and expansion study evaluating darovasertib in combination with crizotinib (the darovasertib combination) in patients with solid tumors harboring GNAQ/11 mutations. The ESMO update focuses on the Phase 2 expansion results from OptimUM-01 in HLA-A*02:01-positive mUM patients as of a cutoff date of March 23, 2026. A total of 101 patients were evaluated with median follow up of 10.4 months, including 13 treatment naïve patients and 15 patients that received prior tebentafusp as their only systemic treatment prior to the darovasertib combination. Notably, approximately 66% of the patients had received two or more prior lines of therapy. As summarized in the table below, the combination demonstrated an encouraging profile across key measures of efficacy, including overall response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), duration of response (DOR), progression free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS).

| DCR* % (n/N) | 90.9% (10/11) | 85.7% (12/14) | 80.2% (69/86) |

| Median DOR* | 10.2 mos | 5.6 mos | 7.4 mos |

| Median PFS† 95% CI | 7.4 mos 3.6-19.6 | 5.7 mos 3.65-NE | 5.4 mos 3.7-6.8 |

| Median OS† 95% CI | 27.1 mos 8.94-NE | 12.1 mos 9.79-NE | 13.4 mos 9.8-26.3 |

| CI = confidence interval, NE = not estimable * Response assessments utilized efficacy-evaluable population, which includes all patients ≥3 post-baseline assessments or who discontinued treatment; † PFS and OS assessments were based on the total enrolled population, which includes all patients receiving ≥1 dose of treatment |

Based on data from large meta-analyses published by Khoja and Rantala it has been shown that mUM has an especially poor prognosis, with a reported median PFS of 2.8 months and median OS of ~12 months in the treatment-naïve setting. In the 2L setting, median PFS remains at ~2-3 months but median OS drops to ~8 months with a 1-year OS rate of ~37%. As shown in the table above the data from OptimUM-01 compares favorably to these historical PFS and OS benchmarks, as well as to historical ORR which is typically ~5%. Safety was manageable and generally consistent with previously reported results, with the most common treatment-related adverse events of diarrhea (82%), nausea (76%), peripheral edema (70%), and vomiting (57%). Related adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred in 9 (8.9%) participants.

item.titleRaw: 2026 ESMO前瞻丨聚焦TGCT与硬纤维瘤：匹米替尼MANEUVER研究2年随访数据公布，尼罗司他真实世界与剂量策略证据亮相
item.titleZh: 2026 ESMO前瞻丨聚焦TGCT与硬纤维瘤：匹米替尼MANEUVER研究2年随访数据公布，尼罗司他真实世界与剂量策略证据亮相

cases.text:
2026年10月23日至27日，欧洲肿瘤内科学会（ESMO）大会将在西班牙马德里举行。本次ESMO大会上，默克（Merck KGaA）旗下两款产品——口服高选择性CSF-1R抑制剂匹米替尼（Pimicotinib）与靶向γ-分泌酶抑制剂尼罗司他（Nirogacestat）共计5项研究成果入选，聚焦肉瘤（Sarcoma）领域，覆盖腱鞘巨细胞瘤（TGCT）和硬纤维瘤（DT）两大罕见、局部侵袭性疾病。

其中，匹米替尼Ⅲ期MANEUVER研究有2项成果以壁报（Poster）形式展示，包括备受关注的2年长期随访分析及生活质量（EQ-5D-5L）数据；尼罗司他有3项研究成果入选：1项Ⅲ期DeFi研究剂量减少的事后分析以壁报形式展示，2项分别以电子壁报（ePoster）形式展示——包括与索拉非尼历史队列对比的真实世界研究，以及一项晚期DT系统治疗的更新贝叶斯网状Meta分析。

10月19日，2026年ESMO大会常规研究摘要已于官网正式公布，以下为重点内容：

腱鞘巨细胞瘤（TGCT）

▶▶ 匹米替尼治疗腱鞘巨细胞瘤（TGCT）：Ⅲ期MANEUVER试验2年分析

大会报告信息：

■ 报告编号：3747P

■ 展示类型：壁报（Poster）

■ 展示当地时间：10月26日12:00-12:45

■ 展示北京时间：10月26日19:00-19:45

■ 报告人：Hans Gelderblom教授（荷兰莱顿）；中国研究者包括：牛晓辉教授（北京）、徐海荣教授（北京）、李涛教授（杭州）、冯毅教授、张晓晶教授（沈阳）、华莹奇教授、王靖教授、刘傥教授、沈靖南教授、周勇教授

研究核心信息：

TGCT是一种罕见的局部侵袭性肿瘤，持久的症状控制与功能改善仍是关键未满足需求。MANEUVER研究（NCT05804045）此前已在第25周（主要终点）及1年随访中证实，口服高选择性CSF-1R抑制剂匹米替尼在不可切除、有症状TGCT患者中具有快速、强劲的抗肿瘤活性，并带来有意义的症状与功能改善。本次ESMO大会首次公布其2年疗效与安全性分析。

研究将94例患者按2:1随机分配至匹米替尼 50 mg每日一次或安慰剂组（24周双盲期），符合条件者随后进入24周开放标签期及延长期。数据截至2026年3月1日。

结果显示，最初随机至匹米替尼组的63例患者中，54%（n=34）的患者在数据截止时仍在接受治疗。接受匹米替尼治疗的患者中，疗效持续改善：根据RECIST v1.1 标准，客观缓解率（ORR）在第1年与第2年间为76.2%（95% CI 63.8–86.0）；按肿瘤体积评分（TVS），ORR从74.6%（62.1-84.7）升至77.8%（65.5-87.3），中位缓解时间（mDOR）尚未达到；首次评估（第5周）即观察到的症状和关节功能获益持续存在，并在2年时进一步改善[第97周较基线平均变化（SD）]：关节活动度（ROM）+19.6%（27.9）、僵硬−3.9（1.9）、疼痛−3.1（2.1）、躯体功能（PF）+7.4（7.0）。2年数据截止时中位（范围）治疗时长为22.5（1.8–33.6）个月；在治疗的第一年和第二年之间，分别发生1例因TEAE剂量减少和1例停药（累积发生率分别为27%和7.9%），中位剂量强度为85%，安全性与既往分析一致。

结论：在MANEUVER研究中，匹米替尼在所有与患者相关结局（ROM、僵硬、疼痛、躯体功能）方面均取得了早期且有临床意义的改善，并且这些改善持续了2年。肿瘤缓解保持强劲且持久，安全性可控，与既往报道一致。这些数据凸显了匹米替尼减轻这一致残性疾病核心患者负担（其症状和功能障碍会影响患者的日常生活）的能力。

▶▶ 匹米替尼对腱鞘巨细胞瘤患者生活质量的影响：Ⅲ期MANEUVER试验的EQ-5D-5L结果

大会报告信息：

■ 报告编号：3756P

■ 展示类型：壁报（Poster）

■ 展示当地时间：10月26日12:00-12:45

■ 展示北京时间：10月26日19:00-19:45

■ 报告人：Albiruni Ryan Abdul Razak教授（加拿大多伦多）

研究核心信息：

TGCT由集落刺激因子-1（CSF-1）过度表达驱动，导致功能受损、疼痛和生活质量（QoL）下降。本研究报告MANEUVER试验中健康相关生活质量（HRQoL）的EQ-5D-5L结果。入组的94例患者中，92例（匹米替尼组61例，安慰剂组31例）可评估HRQoL，采用英国、加拿大和中国算法计算年龄/性别校正的平均效用值（1=完全健康，0=死亡）。

基线时TGCT患者的HRQoL低于经年龄和性别校正的一般人群（如英国算法效用值仅0.643、加拿大为0.748、中国为0.701）。匹米替尼治疗后，第25周EQ-5D效用值的改善（英国算法+0.135、加拿大算法+0.093、中国算法+0.138）维持至第49周（英国、加拿大、中国算法分别+0.154、+0.098、+0.157）；而安慰剂组至第25周的效用值升高不具临床意义（英国算法 +0.037、加拿大算法 +0.039、中国算法+0.058；范围 +0.037~+0.058）。

结论：在第49周，匹米替尼治疗在各区域算法中均持续改善了患者的HRQoL。这些结果表明，匹米替尼治疗显著改善了患者的症状、身体功能及日常生活能力，为其在TGCT患者中具有持久疗效提供了有力支持。

硬纤维瘤（DT）

▶▶ 剂量减少对尼罗司他治疗硬纤维瘤患者安全性和疗效的影响：DeFi试验事后分析

大会报告信息：

■ 报告编号：3741P

■ 展示类型：壁报（Poster）

■ 展示当地时间：10月26日12:00-12:45

■ 展示北京时间：10月26日19:00-19:45

■ 报告人：Bruno Vincenzi教授（意大利罗马）

研究核心信息：

DT是一种罕见、局部侵袭性的软组织肿瘤，伴随沉重的症状负担。尼罗司他是唯一获FDA、欧盟委员会及英国MHRA批准、用于需要系统治疗的进展期DT成人患者的靶向γ-分泌酶抑制剂。在全球多中心、双盲Ⅲ期DeFi试验（NCT03785964）中，尼罗司他 150 mg每日两次（BID）显著改善肿瘤缓解和患者报告结局（PRO）。部分TEAE导致剂量减少至100 mg BID，本分析评估了减量患者的安全性与疗效。

在接受尼罗司他治疗的69例患者中，29例（42%）因TEAE减量至100 mg BID，最常见原因为腹泻（9%），减量多发生在治疗早期（中位时间3个周期）。减量后TEAE发生率和严重程度下降，因TEAE停药率低于未减量者（17% vs 28%）。减量后疗效依然稳定：2年无事件生存率分别为75% vs 79%，ORR分别为48% vs 38%，中位至缓解时间分别为5.6 vs 6.0个月；两组PRO（疼痛、症状严重程度、角色功能、躯体功能）改善幅度相近。PK/PD分析显示较高的尼罗司他暴露量与更高的减量可能性相关，但未发现与较高暴露相关的患者因素。

结论：提示因不良事件尼罗司他从150 mg BID减量至100 mg BID的患者，描述性疗效指标未见明显差异，安全性进一步改善——提示减量策略可在有效管理不良事件的同时，维持临床获益，为尼罗司他的长期治疗提供了更大的灵活空间。

▶▶ 尼罗司他与按疾病控制筛选的索拉非尼历史队列对比：单中心真实世界经验

大会报告信息：

■ 报告编号：3798eP

■ 展示类型：电子壁报（ePoster）

■ 报告人：Irene C. Carrasco Garcia（西班牙塞维利亚）

研究核心信息：

该西班牙单中心回顾性观察研究共纳入28例DT患者（82%女性，中位年龄34岁），肿瘤部位包括四肢（35%）、腹腔内（25%）、腹壁（18%）和躯干（22%）。历史索拉非尼队列为25例治疗期间达到疾病控制的患者（PR率35%，1-2级毒性8%，2例因毒性停药）。

8例接受尼罗司他治疗的患者中，可评估者PR率达42%，疾病控制率（DCR）100%，中位至缓解时间4.8个月——约为索拉非尼队列的一半，且未报告治疗相关毒性。

结论：在这项真实世界研究中，尼罗司他展现出快速且持久的疾病控制效果，并具有良好的安全性。研究将尼罗司他与一组已达到疾病控制的索拉非尼治疗患者的历史队列进行比较，突显了尼罗司他在常规临床实践中观察到的良好疗效和耐受性。

▶▶ 晚期硬纤维瘤系统治疗的疗效与安全性：更新的贝叶斯网状Meta分析

大会报告信息：

■ 报告编号：3803eP

■ 展示类型：电子壁报（ePoster）

■ 报告人：Roberto Carmagnani Pestana教授（巴西圣保罗）

研究核心信息：

DT罕见、局部侵袭且生物学行为异质，多种系统治疗已在进展或难治性疾病中显示活性，但直接对比证据有限。该研究检索PubMed、Embase及CENTRAL（截至2026年4月25日）的随机对照试验（RCT），以安慰剂为参照进行固定效应贝叶斯网状Meta分析，评估ORR、1年和2年PFS及≥3级不良事件。

共纳入4项RCT、365例患者。所有活性治疗均较安慰剂改善ORR，其中γ-分泌酶抑制剂尼罗司他的ORR效应最强（OR 8.20；95% CrI 3.25–23.82），优于聚乙二醇脂质体多柔比星（PLD，OR 4.06）和VEGF-TKI类（索拉非尼/帕唑帕尼，OR 3.65）。PFS方面，1年时PLD估计值最优（OR 0.03），其次为VEGF-TKI（OR 0.05）和尼罗司他（OR 0.18）；2年时排序相似（化疗OR 0.04、VEGF-TKI OR 0.11、尼罗司他 OR 0.25）。安全性方面，所有活性治疗均增加≥3级不良事件，尼罗司他毒性估计值最高（OR 6.13；95% CrI 2.87–13.89），其次为PLD（OR 5.24）和VEGF-TKI（OR 3.26）。

结论：在晚期DT中，系统性治疗方案的疗效均优于慰剂组，其中尼罗司他 在ORR方面显示出最有利的估计值；而PLD/ VEGF-TKIs 在1年和2年固定时间点的PFS方面表现更优。然而，与安慰剂相比，所有活性治疗均与3级及以上不良事件（AEs）风险增加相关。因此在缺乏直接比较证据的情况下，应根据个体情况选择治疗方案。

小结

2026 ESMO大会上，默克两款靶向药物在肉瘤领域共计5项研究成果集中亮相，为TGCT和DT这两类罕见、局部侵袭性疾病的系统治疗提供了多层次的新证据。

在TGCT领域，MANEUVER研究的2年随访分析显示，匹米替尼的肿瘤缓解在第1年至第2年间持续改善（RECIST v1.1评估ORR为76.2%，TVS评估由74.6%升至77.8%），中位缓解持续时间尚未达到；关节活动度、僵硬、疼痛和躯体功能等患者相关结局的早期获益不仅持续存在，且在2年时进一步改善，同时安全性与既往分析一致。同期公布的EQ-5D-5L数据则从生活质量维度提供了补充证据——基线时TGCT患者的HRQoL低于经年龄和性别校正的一般人群，而匹米替尼带来的生活质量改善可持续至第49周。两项研究相互印证，提示匹米替尼的获益从影像学缓解延伸至患者躯体功能与生活质量层面，且具备长期持续性。

在DT领域，三项研究从不同角度丰富了尼罗司他的证据链：DeFi试验事后分析提示，因不良事件从150 mg BID减量至100 mg BID的患者疗效未出现显著性差异、安全性有所改善，为临床剂量管理提供了参考；8例西班牙单中心真实世界研究显示，尼罗司他展现出快速且持久的疾病控制效果，并具有良好的安全性；更新的贝叶斯网状Meta分析则提示，在晚期DT中系统性治疗方案的疗效均优于慰剂组，其中尼罗司他 在ORR方面显示出最有利的估计值，与安慰剂相比，所有活性治疗均与3级及以上不良事件（AEs）风险增加相关，个体化治疗决策仍需权衡疗效与安全性。

总体而言，这5项研究覆盖了从Ⅲ期随机对照长期随访、患者报告结局、用药剂量策略到真实世界验证和间接比较证据的完整链条，相关研究为TGCT与DT的疗效、安全性和患者相关结局提供了循证依据。随着大会期间壁报数据的完整展示，更多细节值得持续关注。
