Research Article

Clinical and economic assessments of a personalized support plan to improve adherence to positive airway pressure therapy in patients with obstructive sleep apnea: a randomized controlled trial in Portugal

https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-10446824/v1

This work is licensed under a CC BY 4.0 License

## Version 1

posted

You are reading this latest preprint version

## Purpose

This multicenter, prospective study evaluated clinical and economic impacts of a personalized support plan for the management of positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy for obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) by home support providers (HSPs).

## Methods

Adults with OSA newly prescribed PAP were randomized to a personalized support plan (VitalCare) or standard follow-up. The primary endpoint was mean daily PAP usage over the first 3 months. Secondary endpoints were proportion of adherers and symptom control after 12 months, medical/provider workload, and estimated health economic impact.

## Results

107 individuals were analyzed (65 males, aged 57.1 years, mean apnea-hypopnea index 30.4/h). Mean 3-month adherence did not differ significantly between personalized plan and standard care groups (4.61 ± 2.24 vs. 3.85 ± 2.62 h/day; p = 0.059). Between-group differences in the proportion of days with PAP usage, individuals with PAP usage ≥ 4 h/day and < 2 h/day at 6 and 12 months significantly favored the personalized support plan. Over one year, patients in the personalized support versus standard follow-up received ≈0.4 additional medical consultations and ≈1 supplemental provider home visit (and 2.4 other interventions). In the personalized support group, the lower the PAP adherence, the higher the number of interventions. Economic modelling estimated that the higher number of adherers on the personalized support plan would translate to direct and indirect annual savings of €255 and €220/person.

## Conclusions

A personalized support plan has the potential to improve adherence to PAP therapy in individuals with OSA managed by HSPs, and modelling suggested that it could contribute to cost savings for the health system.

Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is the most common form of sleep-disordered breathing, affecting up to a billion adults aged 30–69 years worldwide [1]. In Portugal, about 12.5% of adults this age have moderate to severe OSA [1]. Untreated OSA is associated with increased risk of road traffic accidents [2], cardiovascular [3] and metabolic [4] diseases, impaired cognitive function/dementia [5], reduced health-related quality of life [6], and increased all-cause mortality [7].

The preferred treatment for moderate-to-severe OSA is positive airway pressure (PAP) [8]. PAP splints the upper airway open during sleep and reduces the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI), often to normal levels [8]. In Portugal, PAP therapy is indicated for the treatment of moderate (AHI 15–29 events/h) and severe (AHI ≥ 30 events/h) OSA, and mild OSA (AHI 5–14 events/h) with daytime sleepiness and/or cardiovascular comorbidity [9–11]. Equipment supply and installation are performed at home by home support providers (HSPs). The respiratory technician provides training on device use and cleaning, ensures appropriate mask fitting, and performs follow-up (≥ 2 home visits per patient annually) [9–11].

Long-term adherence to PAP is essential for realizing the benefits of therapy [12]. There is a dose-effect relationship between PAP usage and clinical outcomes/healthcare utilization, starting at usage of 2 h/day [13–15]. However, adequate adherence can be difficult to achieve [16], and average PAP usage has remained similar over the last 20 years [17]. In Portugal, the proportion of patients using PAP for ≥ 4 h/day in the first year of therapy is 54%–59% [18, 19].

Interventions supporting patients using PAP therapy are associated with clinically relevant increases in device usage [20]. A personalized patient support plan implemented by the HSP was developed to improve PAP usage without increasing medical workload. The plan considers lifestyle and OSA-/PAP-related factors at therapy initiation to determine the frequency and type of contacts.

This study compared the effects of the personalized support plan versus standard follow-up on PAP adherence, symptom control, healthcare professional/HSP workload, and estimated potential economic impact for the Portuguese health system.

## Study design and randomization

This multicenter (n = 5), prospective, randomized open-label trial (NCT05246449) was conducted in Portugal from November 2021–December 2023. Participants were randomized 1:1 to undergo HSP management of PAP therapy using a personalized support plan (VitalCare, Air Liquide Healthcare) or standard follow-up. Randomization was stratified by study center and baseline OSA severity. Potential participants were provided with study information during a regular medical consultation; those who provided written informed consent were enrolled. The study protocol was approved by the relevant independent ethics committee at each participating site. The trial was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, and European and local laws.

## Study participants

Eligible participants were aged ≥ 18 years, had been diagnosed with OSA and newly prescribed PAP therapy, were using a PAP device allowing remote data transmission, and had VitalAire as their HSP. Key exclusion criteria were: obesity hypoventilation syndrome; other sleep disorders; severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); severe chronic heart failure; and investigator-assessed mental/cognitive inability to use all personalized support plan components.

Abstract

Background:Hypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) timeseries metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes.

Methods: Blood pressure (n= 560) and HR(n=680) timeseries data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on timeseries data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes.

Results: Successful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes.

Conclusion: Post-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

Introduction

Aortic dissection (AD) is the most common fatal event involving the aorta and occurs in 5 to 30cases per million of the population, resulting in approximately 12,000 deaths annually in the United States. In an acute AD, blood penetrates the aortic wall at the site of an intimal tear and proceeds to separate the aortic layers and extend up or down the aorta, creating a false lumen. This creates a problem of mechanical failure as the aorta, a composite pressurized tube, undergoes interfacial fracture. While surgical management has rapidly evolved in the advent of endovascular therapies, understanding this problem requires knowledge of mechanical factors such as aortic wall stress, aortic shape, and aberrant blood flow patterns.2-5As a result, AD is a mechanical problem best understood through the use of geometry and hemodynamics.

Hypertension is a well-known risk factor for the propagation of type B aortic dissections and rupture. Clinical practice guidelines suggest maintaining a systolic blood pressure (SBP) below130 mmHg for all patients to improve aortic outcomes and overall mortality.6 This is typically monitored in the outpatient setting using a single blood pressure reading that is known to vary substantially from visit to visit due to random variation around the patient's "true"blood pressure owing to measurement errors.7There is limited data on blood pressure immediately following surgical and/or endovascular repair, resulting in attempts to meet the guideline-directed blood pressure target. However, the more frequent collection of data could provide more information leading to a better understating of the behavior of blood pressure following endovascular repair, especially in the most critical 24 hours post-surgery. While temporal patterns are complex8, metrics such as blood pressure variability have been associated with higher risk of cardiovascular events and mortality. cases.text: Abstract Objectives Mindfulness-based cognitive therapy (MBCT) has rarely been tested in non-Western inpatient services or delivered by nurses. This trial evaluated a culturally adapted, nurse-led group MBCT programme for Thai inpatients. Method Ninety-four inpatients with moderate to severe ICD-10 depressive disorder at a Thai psychiatric hospital were randomised 1:1 to MBCT plus routine nursing care or routine care alone. The programme comprised six group sessions of 60–90 minutes over three weeks. Depressive symptoms (9Q), rumination (RRS) and mindfulness (MAS) were assessed before and after the intervention and at three months; readmission within three months of discharge was recorded. Sixteen completers took part in two focus groups (content analysis). Results The arms were equivalent at baseline. Time × Group interactions favoured MBCT on all three outcomes (all p < .001; partial η² = .13–.40). Both arms improved, but at three months MBCT showed lower depressive symptoms (mean difference 3.49, 95% CI [2.75, 4.23], d = 1.93), lower rumination ( d = 3.34) and higher mindfulness ( d = 2.16). Rumination gains were fully maintained after discharge ( p = 1.000) whereas controls deteriorated; mindfulness eroded partially in both arms. Minimal-symptom status was reached by 51.1% of MBCT participants versus 2.1% of controls ( p < .001), a number needed to treat of 2.0. Readmission was less frequent under MBCT (2 of 47 versus 7 of 47) but not significantly so (Fisher's exact p = .158). Three themes emerged: recognising emotions and automatic thoughts; behavioural change with self-compassion; and stress management for relapse prevention. Conclusions Brief, nurse-led, culturally adapted MBCT added clinically meaningful benefit to routine inpatient care, sustained to three months. The trial was underpowered for readmission. Partial erosion of mindfulness gains suggests booster contact may be needed. Preregistration TCTR20250927009, Registration date: September 27, 2025

肝细胞癌是各类慢性肝病患者的主要死因之一。我国肝癌患者 5 年相对生存率仅为 14.4%，I 期确诊占比仅为 17.5%，早期诊断不足在基层和农村地区尤其突出。在基层医疗机构规范开展肝癌筛查，是提高肝癌早期诊断率、改善患者预后的重要环节。《基层医疗机构肝癌筛查专家共识（2026 年）》围绕筛查人群、筛查方法、筛查流程及组织实施提出 16 条推荐意见，为基层医疗机构开展肝癌筛查提供了具体参考。

图源：文献信息截图

（一）先识别：哪些人属于肝癌风险人群？

肝癌筛查并不是对所有人群进行无差别检查，而是应先识别慢性肝病患者，再根据是否合并肝硬化、肝癌家族史等因素进行风险分层。

推荐意见 1：中国成年一般人群应积极筛查常见慢性肝病，主要包括慢性 HBV、HCV感染、酒精性肝病、MAFLD（A1）。

推荐意见 2：各种病因所致的慢性肝病患者均为肝癌的风险人群，可以简单分为一般风险人群和高危风险人群。其中存在肝硬化、有肝癌家族史的慢性肝病患者属于肝癌的高危风险人群（B1）。

共识指出，肝硬化是肝癌发生的主要危险因素，80% 以上的肝癌病例发生于肝硬化基础上。除肝硬化和肝癌家族史外，基层医生还应重点询问病毒性肝炎、饮酒情况、代谢相关疾病及既往肝功能异常等信息。风险评估时可重点关注以下情况：

病毒感染：HBV 感染、HCV 感染；

饮酒情况：男性每日饮酒量 ＞ 40 g、女性 ＞ 20 g，且持续 5 年以上；

代谢因素：超重或肥胖、高血压、糖尿病、血脂异常；

肝脏情况：肝硬化、肝功能异常、肝癌家族史。

推荐意见 10：根据病史采集、体格检查及常规化验检查可初步识别肝癌风险人群；结合相关诊断标准可明确肝癌风险人群；结合慢性肝病患者是否存在肝癌家族史和/或是否符合肝硬化诊断标准，可判断出肝癌高危风险人群（A1）。

（二）再分层：基层如何判断肝硬化风险？

肝硬化是肝癌发生的重要危险因素。对于基层医疗机构而言，可先通过病史、体格检查、常规化验及简便的无创指标进行初步筛查，再结合超声和肝脏硬度检测进一步判断。

推荐意见 3：天冬氨酸氨基转移酶/血小板比值指数（APRI） 和 纤维化-4 指数（FIB-4）可用于基层医疗机构的肝硬化筛查。针对慢性肝病患者自动计算并直接出具报告，方便其在基层医疗机构的推广应用（A1）。

推荐意见 4：慢性肝病患者 APRI＞1 或 FIB-4＞1.3 时，应考虑肝硬化可能，需影像学如超声、振动控制瞬时弹性成像进一步判别；APRI ＞2 或 FIB-4 ＞2.67 时，考虑肝硬化可能性较高，建议纳入高危管理（B1）。

共识给出了两项指标的计算方法：APRI＝（AST/AST正常值上限）÷血小板计数（10⁹/L）×100。FIB-4 ＝ 年龄 ×AST÷［血小板计数（10⁹/L）×√ALT］（AST 为天冬氨酸氨基转移酶，ALT 为丙氨酸氨基转移酶）。两项指标主要用于慢性肝病基础上的肝硬化初筛，并不适合脱离临床背景单独判断。AST 和血小板计数还可能受到急性肝损伤、肌肉损伤、药物、血液系统疾病等因素影响，因此出现异常结果后，仍需结合超声、振动控制瞬时弹性成像及其他临床资料进一步判断。

表 1 APRI 和 FIB-4 的基层应用

（三）肝脏硬度如何判断？

推荐意见 6：振动控制瞬时弹性测定技术可用于各类病因肝硬化的诊断，但需注意高胆红素、高 ALT 等特殊情况对检测值的影响（A1）。

推荐意见 7：不同病因肝硬化患者的瞬时弹性测定阈值存在差异，但基层医疗机构可将振动控制瞬时弹性测定的肝脏硬度值 ＞12.0 kPa 作为识别各类病因肝硬化（F4 期）的统一阈值，用于指导个体化筛查周期的制定（B1）。

（四）怎么查：腹部超声联合AFP

推荐意见 5：慢性肝病患者应将 AFP 作为筛查肝癌的常规血清标志物（A1）。有条件的医疗机构可联合检测 AFP-L3 和 DCP，由此自动计算生成的 C-GALAD 有助于提高肝癌早期诊断率（B1）。

推荐意见 8：腹部超声是现阶段基层医疗机构诊断肝硬化最简便可行的影像学检查方法，联合血清 AFP 是肝癌一线筛查方案（B1）。

共识引用的研究显示，AFP 单独用于早期肝癌筛查时，敏感度和特异度均存在局限；AFP-L3 和 DCP 联合应用后，可进一步提高对肝癌的识别能力。由 AFP、AFP-L3和DCP 等指标联合构建的C-GALAD模型，在相关研究中显示出较好的鉴别能力。但 AFP-L3、DCP 及 C-GALAD 并非基层所有患者的常规必查项目，应根据医疗机构条件选择应用。

腹部超声具有操作简便、价格较低和可重复性较好的特点，适合基层开展。但其检查效果会受到设备性能、操作者经验、患者体型、肝脏位置及病灶大小等因素影响。增强 CT 或增强 MRI 不作为基层普通人群的常规筛查手段，而主要用于以下情况：超声发现肝脏结节；超声发现非典型占位性病变；肝脏血清肿瘤标志物异常；超声检查质量不佳，无法完成有效判断；需要进一步明确肝脏病变性质。

（五）多久查一次：根据风险分层安排频率

推荐意见 11：所有风险人群均应定期进行肝癌筛查，一般风险人群至少每年筛查 1 次，高危风险人群至少每 3～6 个月筛查 1 次（B1）。

推荐意见 12：对于肝癌高危风险患者，若超声显示肝内疑似癌前病变或非典型占位性病变，或肝脏血清肿瘤标志物异常，应尽快行增强影像学检查；如未明确诊断肝癌，建议每 3 个月筛查 1 次，每 6 个月行增强影像学检查（B1）。

（六）发现异常：基层何时需要转诊？

推荐意见 9：基层医疗机构对于超声发现肝脏结节和/或肝癌血清标志物异常的患者，应转诊至县区级医疗机构，必要时进行增强影像学检查，以完成早期肝癌的精准诊断（A1）。

基层医疗机构的主要任务包括：1. 识别慢性肝病患者；2. 完成肝癌风险分层；3. 开展腹部超声和 AFP 筛查；4. 识别异常结果；5. 及时完成转诊。

（七）三级联动：村筛、乡查、县诊

推荐意见13：以乡镇、社区医疗机构为中心，建立村筛（村医/家庭医生）-乡查（乡镇、社区医疗机构）-县诊（县区级医疗机构）三级联动的筛查管理机制（C1）。

推荐意见14：村医/家庭医生负责初筛慢性肝病患者；乡镇、社区医疗机构负责进一步确认慢性肝病，尽可能区别肝癌一般风险/高危风险人群，高危人群或无法判定风险者及时转诊；县区级医疗机构应设立感染/肝病或消化专科，负责进一步确认肝硬化、肝癌及辖区内技术培训（B1）。

不同层级医疗机构应各有侧重，见表 2：

对于已经明确诊断的肝病患者，基层医疗机构还应开展规律随访、健康教育和复查提醒；对于疑似肝硬化、无法判断风险或出现异常检查结果的患者，应及时转诊。

（八）健康教育和慢病管理同样重要

推荐意见15：基层医疗机构均有责任针对普通公众及慢性肝病患者开展规范化肝癌早筛健康教育。依托多元载体与健康宣传节点，持续普及肝癌早筛理念，推动形成「早筛早诊、主动参与、应筛尽筛」的基层防控氛围（B1）。

肝癌筛查并非一次性检查。基层医疗机构还应帮助患者了解慢性肝病与肝癌风险之间的关系，明确筛查项目、筛查频率以及异常结果后的复诊和转诊要求。建议 18 岁以上人群至少接受一次 HBV 相关检测，并根据病史和临床表现进一步开展相关检查。

推荐意见16：积极健全基层医疗机构慢病管理体系，充分发挥现有慢病管理网络作用，将慢性肝病纳入其中。完善并依托信息化管理系统与远程会诊，补齐基层医疗资源短板，提高基层医生肝癌筛查与管理水平（C2）。

基层肝癌筛查应与慢性肝病长期管理相结合，纳入健康档案、家庭医生签约、门诊随访及远程会诊体系，做好筛查结果登记、定期随访提醒、异常结果追踪以及转诊复诊记录。在医疗资源有限的地区，可通过信息化管理系统、远程会诊及便携式超声设备，提高基层筛查的可及性和连续性。

临床速记：慢性肝病患者属于肝癌风险人群；肝硬化和肝癌家族史提示高危风险；

APRI、FIB-4 可用于基层初筛肝硬化；APRI ＞1 或 FIB-4 ＞1.3 时，应进一步检查；

APRI ＞2 或 FIB-4＞2.67 时，建议纳入高危管理；腹部超声联合 AFP 是一线筛查方案；一般风险人群至少每年筛查 1 次；高危风险人群至少每 3～6 个月筛查 1 次；发现肝脏结节或肿瘤标志物异常，应及时转诊；肝癌筛查应纳入慢性肝病长期管理。

证据分级说明：本共识采用 GRADE 证据分级和推荐强度分级。证据质量分为高质量（A）、中等质量（B）、低质量（C）和极低质量（D）；推荐强度分为强推荐（1）和弱推荐（2）。

✩ 本文仅供医疗卫生等专业人士参考

《分枝杆菌感染实验诊断标准》解读.pdf 下载请点击： AI指南解读 评论区 (0) 中国医学科学院 · 2022-04-29 中国医学科学院病原生物学研究所 · 2022-01-10 作者报告了一例因咬肌肥大注射肉毒毒素后皮肤脓肿分枝杆菌感染的病例，并回顾了过去十年中美容注射后NTM感染的文献。 今天我们学习一系列的八名患者偶然分枝杆菌感染的案例。感染与一个单一的纹身管理机构有关。每个患者在临床表现和实验室检查结果方面都是独特的，但是他们的共同点是都感染了偶然分枝杆菌。 高风险非肌肉侵入型膀胱癌（BC）的标准治疗方法是膀胱内注射牛型结核菌BCG。之前的研究表明了可以通过非病原性分枝杆菌，比如布鲁姆分枝杆菌和/或者不同的分枝杆菌传输形式，比如橄榄油-水状乳液均能改善上述治疗效果。虽然之前的研究已经阐释了BCG治疗能够激活免疫系统，而改变分枝杆菌和/或者准备方式对免疫效果的影响仍旧未知。最近，有研究人员在一个原位小鼠BC模型中，通过流式细胞术和multiplexing 结核分枝杆菌是结核病（TB）的病原体，主要引起肺损伤和结节。尽管通常认为巨噬细胞是携带结核分枝杆菌的主要细胞，但新的证据表明嗜中性粒细胞迅速募集到受感染的肺部。结核分枝杆菌本身或其早期分泌的抗原靶蛋白6（ESAT-6）可以诱导嗜中性粒细胞胞外诱集剂（NETs）的形成。然而，NETs仅能捕获却无法杀死分枝杆菌，其在分枝杆菌发病机制中的作用尚不清楚。在这里，我们报告了一种新的结核分枝杆菌细胞外因子，双 2012年，一种神秘的细菌开始在一小部分刚接受了心脏直视手术的患者中出现。在3年的时间里，这种引发肺结核的病原体的“远亲”——分枝杆菌嵌合体在全球感染了至少49人，并且导致一大半患者死亡。虽然科学家最终将疾病的发作追查到心脏手术期间使用的受污染的医疗设备，但分枝杆菌嵌合体最初是如何污染设备的仍不清楚。如今，一项最新研究表明，感染可能源自设备在德国的生产地。“这是一项非常吸引人的工作。研究人员在将感 cases.text:
Recall of DANTRIUM 20 mg Powder for Solution for Injection

21 October 2026

Audiences

Healthcare professional

Product-type

Therapeutic Products

Retail-level recall of one batch of DANTRIUM 20 mg Powder for Solution for Injection, containing dantrolene, due to presence of visible foreign particulate matter in the vials.

Recall details

| Date of recall: | 20 October 2026 |

| Product: | DANTRIUM 20 mg Powder for Solution for Injection |

| Active Ingredient: | Dantrolene |

| Product Category: | Therapeutic Product |

| Batch No.: | 80681 |

| Class of Recall: | 1 |

| Level of Recall: | Retail |

| Local Company: | Alliance Pharm Pte Ltd |

| Description of Issue: | Presence of visible foreign particulate matter in the vials. The affected batch is recalled as a precautionary measure. |

| Recall Instructions: | Hospitals, clinics, pharmacies: Stop supplying the affected batch and return the remaining stocks to the company. |

Note:

The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) publishes information regarding recalls of health products supplied in Singapore. These product recalls may be conducted on a company’s own initiative or upon HSA’s request to remove products where there are issues with quality, safety or efficacy.

When a recall is initiated, it does not necessarily imply that a product is considered unsafe or is inefficacious. A recall can also be initiated to remove products with quality defects that does not impact safety or efficacy from the market so as to ensure that products registered in Singapore continue to meet the stringent regulatory standards stipulated by HSA.

Not all recalls will be publicly announced via press releases. When a recall involves a product that has been widely distributed or a product that poses a serious health risk, HSA will update the public through its channels, which may include its website, social media platforms or a press release.

Class of recall

A recall is classified as Class 1 or Class 2 depending on the potential hazard of the issue.

- Class 1: For recalls of products with issues that can potentially cause serious adverse health outcomes or death.

- Class 2: For recalls of products with issues that would not likely cause serious adverse health outcomes.

Level of recall

The level of product recall will depend on the potential hazard of the affected product, extent of distribution and whether other mitigating measures can be taken to address the issue.

- Consumer level: Affected product or batch(es) recalled from patients and consumers as well as wholesale suppliers, retail suppliers, hospitals, clinics and pharmacies.

- Retail level: Affected product or batch(es) recalled from retail suppliers, hospitals, clinics and pharmacies as well as wholesale suppliers.

- Wholesale level: Affected product or batch(es) recalled from wholesale suppliers.

cases.text:
Health Sciences Authority Strengthens Local and Global Partnerships to Accelerate Healthcare Innovations

12 October 2026

Audiences

Consumer

Healthcare professional

Industry member

The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) announced three initiatives to help promising healthcare innovations reach patients sooner: (i) collaboration with the United Kingdom’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) through the Regulatory Innovation Corridor on regulatory considerations for breakthrough therapies that use Artificial Intelligence (AI) in drug development and clinical trials; (ii) a common entry point for clinical research and regulatory engagement in Singapore; and (iii) a HSA-Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE) Priority Track that will allow selected health products to undergo regulatory evaluation and health technology assessment concurrently. The initiatives could halve approval times for selected lower-risk Phase 3 clinical trials from 30 days to 15 days and shorten the time for the first health technology assessment decision from about one year to six to nine months after regulatory approval. They were announced at the opening of the inaugural Health Regulatory Conference 2026 on 12 October 2026.

2 Speaking at the event, Guest-of-Honour Mr Ong Ye Kung, Minister for Health and Coordinating Minister for Social Policies, outlined how HSA’s regulatory approach is expanding across geographical boundaries, the healthcare value chain and regulatory domains. By working with industry, healthcare institutions and professionals as well as international partners, HSA aims to reinforce and strengthen the healthcare ecosystem and establish Singapore’s position as a trusted regulatory hub, and thus help beneficial innovations reach patients sooner.

Trusted Regulator and Gateway to Global Markets

3 HSA is internationally recognised as a trusted regulator and reference agency. It became the first national regulatory authority in the world to attain the World Health Organization's (WHO) highest Maturity Level (ML4) for medical devices regulatory systems in 2026. HSA also holds WHO's highest recognition for medicines regulatory systems, the WHO Listed Authority, and is recognised as a WHO Stringent Regulatory Authority for high-risk in-vitro diagnostics. Singapore is also a member of the Access Consortium, alongside Australia, Canada, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, that aligns regulatory practices, shares the work of evaluating therapeutic products and makes better use of scarce expertise.

4 Building on these achievements, HSA is working towards the WHO Listed Authority status for vaccines — the highest level under the WHO's regulatory benchmarking framework. This is critical to Singapore’s pandemic prevention, preparedness and response efforts, potentially speeding up access to vaccines while maintaining high safety standards.

Building Capabilities and Strengthening the Healthcare Ecosystem to Future-proof Regulation

5 As AI is increasingly applied throughout the drug-development lifecycle, HSA is strengthening its capabilities and developing regulatory guidance for the healthcare sector. To support innovators in this rapidly evolving field, HSA has partnered with the United Kingdom’s Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) to establish a Regulatory Innovation Corridor. This corridor will speed up patient access to breakthrough therapies, including those that use AI in drug development and clinical trials, by providing innovators with a coordinated pathway to engage with both regulators at the same time. This can help them plan ahead, design better clinical trials, avoid duplication and reduce delays. HSA and MHRA will also share regulatory approaches, advance regulatory innovation, and give innovators clearer and more predictable expectations across markets.

6 Singapore will also strengthen support across the healthcare value chain, from clinical development and regulatory evaluation to health technology assessment and patient access. Since July 2026, Enterprise Singapore, the Economic Development Board, HSA and the Singapore Clinical Research Institute (SCRI) have been working to coordinate a common entry point for clinical research and regulatory engagement in Singapore. This will be launched in early 2027 to provide more coordinated support for industry sponsors. Separately, HSA will streamline regulatory review processes, leading to faster approvals. For instance, approval times for selected lower-risk Phase 3 clinical trials may be halved from 30 days to 15 days. This strengthens Singapore's attractiveness as a clinical trials hub.

7 From November 2026, HSA and the Agency for Care Effectiveness (ACE) will introduce an ACE-HSA Priority Track for selected innovative health products, allowing regulatory evaluation and health technology assessment to be conducted concurrently rather than sequentially. Doing so could shorten the time needed for the first health technology assessment decision from about one year to six to nine months after regulatory approval. Regulatory and health technology assessment decisions will remain independent, and existing high standards for safety and clinical effectiveness will not change. (Refer to www.go.gov.sg/ace-hsa-priority-track (opens in new tab) for more information on ACE-HSA Priority Track).

8 HSA will also establish a Healthcare Industry Advisory Council in the first half of 2027, to bring partners with industry experience to be directly involved in its future planning. The Council will identify emerging opportunities and risks, advise on future capability needs, and provide practical industry perspectives on policy and service design.

9 Together, these initiatives create a faster, more coordinated journey from innovation to care - giving innovators earlier guidance, reducing duplication and helping to bring promising innovations sooner to more patients.

item.titleRaw: Results posted: High Versus Low Power Settings During Ureteroscopic Laser Lithotripsy
item.titleZh: 输尿管镜激光碎石高功率与低功率设置结果公布

cases.text:
背景：钬：钇铝石榴石（Ho:YAG）激光因其多功能性，一直被视为输尿管镜（URS）的金标准激光，能够击碎泌尿道内各种类型的结石，并可进行肿瘤及软组织消融。近期，一种新型铥光纤激光（TFL）被引入，其基础物理特性更为有利。此前的临床前研究预测，在相同功率设置下，TFL 碎石的速度可达 Ho:YAG 碎石的 4 倍。今年早些时候，本研究的研究者发表了首个临床随机试验，比较了使用 TFL 与 Ho:YAG 进行输尿管镜碎石术后的结局。该研究显示，与 Ho:YAG 相比，TFL 获得了更高的无石率（SFR），此外并发症发生率更低、手术时间更短。基于该研究，研究者认为 TFL 正逐渐成为首选激光。在该研究中，使用 TFL 进行 URS 碎石时，极低的激光设置被证明非常高效。然而，对于该手术过程中 TFL 的首选激光设置尚无共识，已提出了多种不同的设置，包括高达 45 瓦（W）的高功率设置。

迄今为止，尚无临床随机试验比较 TFL 的不同激光设置，以确定在临床结局方面何为最佳。

研究目的：本研究的主要目的是比较使用 TFL 以低功率和高功率设置进行肾结石 URS 碎石术后的手术时间。次要目的是比较低功率和高功率设置在 SFR、激光时间、激光激活模式、术中及术后并发症方面的结果。

研究设计：本研究计划为前瞻性随机试验。所有 ≥ 18 岁、计划在 Haukeland 大学医院（HUH）日间手术单元接受 8-25 mm 肾结石 URS 碎石术的患者均被邀请入组研究。在签署书面知情同意书后，患者被随机分配至采用低功率或高功率激光设置的 URS TFL 碎石术。

激光设置：两个研究组的激光设置是标准化的，并且需要在手术全程中保持不变。

第 1 组 - 低功率（4-6W），短脉冲：0.4 - 0.6 焦耳（J），10 赫兹（Hz） 第 2 组 - 高功率（16-18W），短脉冲：0.4 J / 40 Hz 0.6 J / 30 Hz 0.8 J / 20 Hz

第 1 组（低功率）的标准启动设置为 0.4J / 10Hz（4W），第 2 组（高功率）为 0.4J / 40Hz（16W）。

URS 手术：URS 手术在全身麻醉下进行，手术开始前将根据科室指南给予预防性抗生素，依据尿培养或当前当地方案。

手术从膀胱镜检查开始，随后在认为合适时进行半硬性输尿管镜（URS）。安全导丝和通道鞘可由术者酌情使用，但在 HUH 的 URS 中通常省略。必要时行球囊扩张。内镜检查可使用半硬性和软性输尿管镜。整个手术过程使用室温、60 cm 高度的重力灌注液。到达结石时，打开揭示随机分组结果为高或低激光设置的密封信封。可使用 150μm 激光光纤进行碎石。使用 TFL 按照下述预定义设置并根据随机分组对结石进行粉碎。为使手术过程尽可能相似，结石应被粉末化/粉碎至尽可能小的颗粒，而不是被击碎后取出。手术结束时仅可取出不适合进一步粉碎的残留颗粒，以使患者无结石残留。

术后如认为必要，可放置双 J 支架；若放置，则按标准常规在 1-2 周后于门诊取出。

随访：所有患者在术后 3 个月接受计算机断层扫描（CT）随访，以评估无结石状态并排除输尿管狭窄，同时进行临床咨询。

伦理考量与批准：所有符合纳入研究条件的患者将获得口头和书面信息。参与研究是自愿的，患者可在研究过程中的任何时间点选择退出。只有在签署知情同意书后才会纳入研究。

本研究已获挪威国家研究伦理委员会批准（REK：550740）。此外，已向豪克兰大学医院数据保护机构提交批准申请。

before.summary: 挪威 Haukeland University Hospital 公布了输尿管镜铥光纤激光碎石高功率与低功率设置随机试验的结果，入组 150 例。研究主要比较两种功率设置下的手术时间，次要比较结石清除率、激光时间、激光激活模式及术中术后并发症，患者为 8-25 mm 肾结石。
before.lead: 挪威Haukeland大学医院的研究者公布了一项前瞻性随机试验结果，比较输尿管镜碎石术中铥光纤激光（TFL）高功率与低功率设置的效果。研究纳入≥18岁、肾结石8-25 mm、拟行日间手术输尿管镜碎石的患者，随机分为低功率组（4-6W，0.4-0.6 J、10 Hz）和高功率组（16-18W，0.4 J/40 Hz、0.6 J/30 Hz、0.8 J/20 Hz），主要终点为手术时间，次要终点包括结石清除率、激光时间、激光激活模式及围手术期和术后并发症。术后3个月行CT评估结石清除状态并排除输尿管狭窄。研究经挪威国家科研伦理委员会批准（REK: 550740）。

item.titleZh: 孕产妇阿片使用障碍照护模式研究结果登记

cases.text:
新英格兰北部是美国阿片类药物依赖率最高的地区之一，患病率在18-35岁人群中最高且仍在增长。该地区围产期阿片类药物使用障碍（OUD）的发生率反映了这一公共卫生危机；新英格兰北部地区是全国阿片类药物相关出生发生率最高的地区。在缅因州、新罕布什尔州和佛蒙特州，围产期阿片类药物使用障碍影响5-8%的妊娠，这3个州受到当前阿片类药物流行的严重影响。OUD治疗不充分的后果包括早产和其他围产期并发症、新生儿因新生儿戒断（NAS）而延长住院时间，以及孕产妇因感染性疾病和过量用药导致的患病和死亡。2013年，美国与NAS治疗相关的费用达到15亿美元。自2013年以来，这一流行已增长数倍。

使用美沙酮或丁丙诺啡的药物辅助治疗（MAT）是妊娠期推荐的标准治疗。包括美国妇产科医师学会（ACOG）、美国儿科学会、母胎医学会和美国成瘾医学学会在内的专业机构，已呼吁采用促进OUD孕妇早期识别和治疗的照护模式。转诊至MAT专科项目一直是公认的标准治疗，已证明对妇女及其婴儿安全。然而，为应对不断升级的阿片类药物危机，ACOG开始向其成员提供丁丙诺啡培训项目。因此，新英格兰北部许多产科照护机构现在提供整合式MAT服务。但即使存在此类整合项目，关于为OUD孕妇提供MAT的最佳照护模式仍存在疑问。

存在患者和提供者因素，与何种MAT模式对何人最有效的效果差异相关。对女性而言，丁丙诺啡相对于美沙酮的优势包括过量风险较低、药物相互作用较少、可在产科照护背景下获得诊室治疗服务，以及已证明的NAS病程较短。丁丙诺啡相对于美沙酮的劣势包括潜在的肝功能障碍、缺乏关于胎儿暴露对婴儿后果的长期数据、对成瘾严重程度高的患者疗效可能有限、需要在开始治疗前有中度戒断症状以避免医源性戒断，以及转移（即分享或出售）风险增加。尽管丁丙诺啡已证明具有新生儿方面的优势，但并非对所有女性都有效。美沙酮治疗的结构（每日会面）也可能更好地契合某些女性的支持需求。对提供者而言，选择向患者提供何种药物辅助治疗方式，往往受限于专科照护服务的可用性和可及性。

比较整合式与转诊式 MAT 照护模式在产后治疗留存及女性在这两种模式中的体验方面的有效性的文献有限。特别是，成瘾严重程度高或合并心理健康状况的女性，其产前照护需求可能不同于行为健康问题较不复杂的女性。研究也尚未评估母亲阿片类成瘾严重程度对新生儿结局和母亲长期康复的影响。为母亲提供最适当、最有效的治疗，才能实现最佳的新生儿结局。

患者、提供者和其他利益相关者面临的挑战是确定在孕期和分娩后提供 MAT 以改善结局的最佳方法。目前，各地区产科实践提供以下两种方式之一：(1) 整合式照护，即 MAT 及相关心理社会服务与产科照护在同一地点提供；(2) 转诊式照护，即女性在分开的专门地点接受 MAT 和产科照护。对于 OUD 母亲及其婴儿而言，这两种模式在 MAT、产科及其他所需服务的可及性、可获得性、可接受性和质量，以及分娩后的长期随访和治疗方面，各有不同的潜在优势和劣势。虽然妊娠促使女性启动 MAT，但阿片类物质使用复发和 MAT 中断常发生在产后第 1 年内，使母亲和婴儿均面临重大风险。支付方和政策制定者也在寻求答案，即应将医疗资源投向何处以增加孕妇获得治疗的机会，尤其是在当前的阿片类危机中。OUD 女性中通过 Medicaid 系统参保的比例过高；Medicaid 政策影响女性获得广泛服务的机会，从当日服务或照护协调的报销，到女性在分娩后是否继续符合福利资格。

研究目的：本研究的主要目的旨在通过比较缅因州、新罕布什尔州和佛蒙特州目前临床使用的两种 MAT 提供模式在患者照护体验以及围产期、新生儿和较长期物质使用治疗结局方面的真实世界有效性，来回答这些重要的患者、提供者和政策问题。将探讨以下主要的比较效果研究 (CER) 患者中心结局研究所 (PCORI) 优先问题：

(1) 孕妇和育儿女性的临床结局和患者报告结局在整合式与转诊式 MAT 实践模式之间是否存在差异？

为回答此问题，将探讨以下主要具体目的：

目的 1（临床结局回顾性研究）。利用临床记录数据评估整合式与转诊式 MAT 照护模式对母婴结局的比较效果。

目标 2（患者报告结局前瞻性研究）。利用患者报告的数据，评估整合式照护模式与转诊式照护模式在以患者为中心的结局方面的比较效果。

研究描述：本研究将与北新英格兰地区提供产科照护的 26 家诊所协作，涵盖整合式照护与转诊式照护模式的实例。研究人群为从上述任何一家诊所接受产前保健、且符合《精神障碍诊断与统计手册》（DSM-5）阿片类药物使用障碍诊断标准的孕妇。将采用基于整群的观察性混合方法设计，比较在通过以下两种服务模式之一提供 MAT 的产科诊所中接受产前保健的阿片类药物使用障碍孕妇的结局：整合式或转诊式。将使用在合作诊所接受产前保健的阿片类药物使用障碍孕妇的回顾性临床记录数据（n=2000）来检验目标 1。目标 2 将通过一个患者报告子样本队列（n=532）来探讨，该队列在照护第 3 个孕期招募，并通过自我报告在线调查随访至产后 6 个月。分析策略将考虑整群效应和患者基线差异，以比较各组的结局。

before.summary: 美国 Dartmouth College 申办的 MOms in REcovery（MORE）观察性研究已完成并登记结果，入组 2,510 人，比较在产科照护中整合药物辅助治疗与转诊至专科项目两种模式对母婴结局的影响。研究同时关注心理健康、照护协调与育儿教育等现场服务的作用，以及产后治疗留存问题。
before.reason: 研究比较孕期阿片使用障碍两种药物辅助治疗照护模式及现场支持服务的作用，可供开展孕产妇成瘾整合照护的机构在设计服务流程与随访方案时参考。
before.lead: 美国北新英格兰地区26家产科诊所登记了一项观察性研究结果，比较阿片使用障碍（OUD）孕妇接受整合式给药（在产科诊所内提供药物辅助治疗MAT及心理社会服务）与转诊式给药（MAT与产科服务分设）两种模式的真实世界效果。研究采用整群观察性混合方法设计：回顾性病历数据纳入2000例OUD孕妇，评估母婴临床结局；另招募532例孕妇，于孕晚期入组并随访至产后6个月，通过在线自报问卷评估以患者为中心的结局。原文未给出具体结果数据。该研究针对的是孕期MAT最优照护模式这一尚未解决的问题，其结果可为产科诊所如何配置MAT服务、以及Medicaid等支付方如何投入资源提供依据。
